title: Binance Warns of Fake Compensation Offers as Withdrawals Resume
summary: Binance warned that impersonators could exploit its withdrawal restart with fake compensation offers and fees for faster processing. The exchange also completed a cryptographic reserve proof, enabling customers to check backing for 10 tokens while recovery continued. Fake Compensation Offers Accompa...
content:
Binance warned that impersonators could exploit its withdrawal restart with fake compensation offers and fees for faster processing. The exchange also completed a cryptographic reserve proof, enabling customers to check backing for 10 tokens while recovery continued.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance rejected paid withdrawal priority and compensation claim links.
  • The completed proof lets customers check backing without exposing balances.
  • Less liquid tokens account for the remaining 5% of affected assets to replenish.

Fake Compensation Offers Accompany Withdrawal Restart

Binance addressed potential fraud during its withdrawal restart following the $6.3 billion hack in a Nov. 2 withdrawal scam warning on X. The exchange stated:

“Withdrawals are resuming in phases and opportunistic scammers may try to take advantage of this period.”

It described the approaches customers could encounter: “They may impersonate Binance through DMs, emails, group chats and even small transfers with a message attached, offering to ‘speed up withdrawals,’ give ‘priority processing,’ help you ‘claim compensation,’ or move your assets into a ‘Binance vault’.”

The exchange cautioned:

“Anyone promising to expedite it for a fee is scamming you.”

It emphasized that Binance would never initiate contact about accounts or funds, sell places in a withdrawal queue, or charge to unlock a network or asset. Transfers to supposed safe accounts, secured wallets, or any address supplied by an impersonator were also among the requests it warned against.

Requests to connect a wallet, sign a transaction, or authorize access can accompany phishing and counterfeit websites that imitate trusted services. Binance cautioned that authorizations could allow third parties to move assets and that on-chain transactions are usually irreversible. It also ruled out requests for passwords, two-factor authentication codes, or seed phrases, along with unsolicited eligibility, status, or compensation claim links.

Scam Alert Follows $4.65 Billion in Withdrawals

The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has separately warned that refund and recovery scammers impersonate organizations and demand upfront payments or financial information. Binance similarly rejected paid asset recovery services and directed customers with pending withdrawals to check the app. Its official verification page can authenticate channels, accounts, and websites; anyone concerned about account security was advised to change passwords, review settings, and contact in-app support.

The alert came one day after Binance’s initial withdrawal reopening across 15 networks on Nov. 1. Between 06:00 and 15:30 UTC that day, the platform processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals against $1.01 billion in deposits. Net outflows totaled approximately $3.64 billion as customers regained access, while restoration continued for other networks and assets.

Customers Gain Access to Reserve Verification

Separately, Binance’s newly available reserve proof covers the snapshot taken at 00:00 UTC on Oct. 31. Holders of BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC can independently check that balances included in that snapshot were backed at least 1:1. The process confirms inclusion and backing without revealing individual customer balances.

Verification requires logging in through the official Binance website and downloading the verifier to run on the customer’s own computer, using an open-source tool that developers and the public can inspect. The company stressed using trusted devices, protecting login information, and avoiding unofficial reserve websites. It reiterated:

“Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users.”

The company-funded asset replenishment reached 90% on Oct. 31 and approximately 95% by Nov. 1. Less liquid tokens accounted for the outstanding 5%, with industry partners helping source replacements. Binance planned another withdrawal phase for Nov. 3 and a broader reserve snapshot for Nov. 4, followed by an estimated 40 to 50 hours to generate its proof.

title: Binance begins second withdrawal phase, exchange outflows slow
summary: The exchange says additional assets will become available for withdrawal from 04:00 UTC on Tuesday as security checks are completed, following an initial reopening on Sunday.
content:
Binance plans to begin a second phase of cryptocurrency withdrawals on Tuesday, as data shows withdrawal volumes have started to stabilize following last week’s $6.3 billion hack.

Withdrawals for additional assets are scheduled to resume progressively from 04:00 UTC on Tuesday, according to Binance’s latest recovery notice. The rollout follows an initial reopening on Nov. 1.

“Like phase one, reopening will roll out progressively across the assets as security and readiness checks are completed,” said Binance.

The exchange said it was prioritizing tokens based on user demand over the past week. Deposits remain available.

Networks part of the second phase of withdrawals include Binance Smart Chain, Ethereum, Solana, XRP Ledger, Sui, Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron and Base, according to Binance.

Binance’s list of assets planned for withdrawal. Source: Binance

On Monday, Binance said it also reopened withdrawals for several fiat currencies, including the US dollar, United Arab Emirates dirham, Vietnamese dong, Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah, adding to a list of 23 other currencies already available for withdrawal.

Binance exchange outflows slow

Data from DefiLlama shows outflows from the crypto exchange have slowed since Sunday, with net outflows on Monday at $2.57 billion, compared to $6.1 billion the day before.

In a separate security reminder, Binance warned that scammers could exploit the phased reopening by impersonating the exchange and offering accelerated withdrawals, sell priority processing, help users claim compensation or direct them to move assets into a purported “Binance vault,” the exchange said.

“Anyone promising to expedite it for a fee is scamming you,” Binance said.

Related: Binance net outflows surge to $5.8B as withdrawals resume after record hack

title: Provably Fair: The Crypto Gaming Platforms Showcasing the Industry’s Latest Innovation
summary:
When it comes to transparency, crypto gaming platforms are placing one aspect at the heart of their efforts: provably fair technology. There was once a time when platforms would tell
The post Provably Fair: The Crypto Gaming Platforms Showcasing the Industry’s Latest Innovation appeared first on Cry...
content:
When it comes to transparency, crypto gaming platforms are placing one aspect at the heart of their efforts: provably fair technology. There was once a time when platforms would tell players to trust that every result is random. Now, with these systems, there’s a way for them to verify outcomes independently. By applying this technology to their original games, it combines familiar gaming formats with a more transparent approach to game results.

The following crypto platforms are leading the way in showcasing the industry’s latest innovation.

  • Duel
  • Thrill
  • Winna
  • Yeet

Duel

At the forefront of this movement is Duel. Play Duel’s provably fair online games, and you’ll see it is possible to verify the outcomes of its games. That means you can see everything was generated fairly and not simply accept the platform’s word. Before a round, Duel generates a server seed. This is joined by a player-provided client seed and nonce, which increases with each round. It also publishes a SHA-256 hash of the server seed before play, creating a commitment that can be checked later.

After the game, Duel reveals the unhashed server seed. You can compare it with the original hash and verify that the combined seeds and nonce produce the recorded result. This hands you a practical way to check the outcome generation process, with a built-in verifier making the process more accessible. The system applies to each of the 12 “Duel Originals”. Those games also stand out for their 100% RTP, which removes the platform’s mathematical advantage. A one-of-a-kind aspect you won’t find elsewhere, it shows Duel goes to the next level for fair gameplay.

Thrill

Thrill also applies provably fair mechanics to its own in-house games. From Dice to Crash, these titles stick with clear outcomes and straightforward rules. That makes them a natural fit for systems that allow players to check how results are generated. Provably fair technology, naturally, adds a verification layer to the gaming experience. Then with Thrill’s XP progression system and weekly races, there are other reasons for players to return.

Winna

Provably fair is also part of the original games found at Winna. From revealing tiles in Mines to watching a ball bounce through Plinko’s pegs, these in-house titles keep it simple with a decision- or chance-based outcome. The value of provably fair technology here is that players have a way to check results on their own. Like Duel, Winna combines these games with a wider crypto gaming platform and sports-related features for multiple interactive options.

Yeet

Combining sports-related features and crypto gaming with its own originals, Yeet includes in-house creations like Dice and Plinko. As these simple formats place the outcome at the center of the experience, transparency is a key aspect. With its provably fair technology implementation, players gain a method for checking game results. Its originals provide an alternative to its wider selection of third-party titles, while the sports-related section expands the platform beyond its original games.

Provably fair technology gives players a way to verify game outcomes. However, it’s important to highlight that it doesn’t guarantee winning. Even if you check ten wins or ten losses in a row, it plays no part in the next result.

title: Tether Says It Froze Over $1.5B From Binance Hack Within 30 Minutes
summary: Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in stolen USDT within 30 minutes of the Binance hack, blocking access to those funds. The announcement followed the FBI’s attribution of the attack to North Korea. Tether Describes $1.5 Billion Binance Hack Freeze Tether said on Nov. 2 that it had frozen m...
content:
Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in stolen USDT within 30 minutes of the Binance hack, blocking access to those funds. The announcement followed the FBI’s attribution of the attack to North Korea.

Key Takeaways

  • The FBI attributed the theft of more than $6 billion to North Korea.
  • Approximately $729 million in stolen USDT moved before freezes took effect.
  • Tether reported more than $7 billion frozen across secondary market addresses.

Tether Describes $1.5 Billion Binance Hack Freeze

Tether said on Nov. 2 that it had frozen more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the Oct. 29 Binance attack. The company stated that its intervention prevented those assets from being transferred, swapped, or laundered, keeping them beyond the attackers’ reach.

Paolo Ardoino, Tether’s CEO, affirmed:

“Within minutes of the hack, our team had frozen more than $1.5 billion.”

Bo Hines, CEO of Tether’s U.S. stablecoin business, commented: “We moved immediately and stopped more than $1.5 billion from reaching the people behind this attack.”

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the Binance theft to North Korea on Oct. 31, identifying the malicious cyber activity as Tradertraitor, the bureau’s designation for the North Korean cyber activity. Investigators observed stolen assets being converted primarily into ether and anticipated further laundering through decentralized finance platforms and instant swap services, which exchange one cryptocurrency for another. The bureau urged cryptocurrency businesses and infrastructure operators to block transactions involving associated addresses.

Onchain Findings Show Funds Moved Before Freezes

Bitquery’s onchain analysis of the Binance attack placed Tether’s first freeze 37 minutes after the main Ethereum drain and 57 minutes after the first attack transfer. The investigation also traced approximately $729 million in stolen USDT that moved before Tether’s freezes took effect. Most of that amount was swapped into ether and TRX, the cryptocurrency used on the Tron network.

Issuers of stablecoins such as USDT and USDC can restrict transfers involving specified addresses. Tether can block USDT transfers involving those addresses, restricting access to the tokens held there. Returning the assets to victims requires further recovery steps.

Binance separately reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to replace affected assets, excluding approximately $3 billion frozen during the response. Its replacement purchases addressed the exchange’s obligations to users independently of efforts to recover the stolen cryptocurrencies.

Enforcement Actions Extend Beyond Binance

Tether’s April intervention involved a $344 million USDT freeze coordinated with U.S. authorities. The company said its wallet-freezing policy aligns with the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions list. Its latest announcement put its law enforcement relationships at more than 360 agencies across 73 countries.

Following an approximately $285 million April exploit at Drift, a Solana-based cryptocurrency trading platform, Tether committed up to $127.5 million toward its recovery. That commitment formed part of a broader support plan tied to the platform’s recovery and future trading revenue.

Including the Binance intervention, Tether reported more than $7 billion in USDT frozen in secondary market addresses, mostly connected to fraud and theft. Separately, as of Oct. 31, it had helped freeze more than 3,590 wallets holding approximately $1.6 billion for the U.S. Department of Justice, Secret Service, and FBI. It also said approximately $1.2 billion obtained through fraud and theft had been returned to rightful owners and law enforcement through reissuance.

title: What to Do If Your Crypto Card Is Lost, Stolen, or Hacked
summary:
You reach for your wallet and the card is gone. Or worse, your phone buzzes with a payment you did not make. With a normal bank card, you would call
The post What to Do If Your Crypto Card Is Lost, Stolen, or Hacked appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
You reach for your wallet and the card is gone. Or worse, your phone buzzes with a payment you did not make. With a normal bank card, you would call the bank and move on. With a crypto card, the stakes can feel higher, because crypto payments are hard or impossible to reverse.

The good news is that most crypto card problems are fixable if you act quickly and in the right order. The key is understanding what was actually exposed, because a lost card and a hacked wallet are very different problems. Here is exactly what to do in each case.

  • First, Figure Out What Is Actually at Risk
  • If Your Card Is Lost or Stolen
  • If Someone Is Using Your Card Online
  • If Your Account or Wallet Is Hacked
  • Beware of Recovery Scams
  • How to Prevent It Happening Again
  • Frequently Asked Questions

First, Figure Out What Is Actually at Risk

Before you panic, separate the card from the crypto behind it.

SituationWhat is exposedUrgency
Physical card lostThe card number and limitsHigh, but contained
Card details stolen onlineCard paymentsHigh, but contained
App or account login compromisedYour card balance and settingsVery high
Wallet seed phrase exposedEvery coin in that walletCritical

A lost plastic card is usually the least dangerous of these. Someone holding it can try to make card payments, but they cannot empty your wallet with it. A leaked seed phrase is the opposite. Whoever has it controls your funds, and no card freeze will stop them.

If Your Card Is Lost or Stolen

Speed matters most in the first few minutes.

  1. Freeze the card in the app. Nearly every crypto card app has an instant freeze toggle. Use it before anything else, since you can unfreeze it if the card turns up.
  2. Check recent transactions. Look for anything you did not make, and screenshot it.
  3. Contact support. Report the card lost or stolen through the app or the issuer’s official support channel, never a number from a search ad.
  4. Order a replacement. A new card comes with a new number, and the old one is cancelled.
  5. Use the virtual card meanwhile. Many providers issue a virtual card you can add to Apple Pay or Google Pay right away.

Cards that spend directly from your own wallet carry an extra advantage here. With a self-custody Crypto Debit Card, your coins stay in the wallet you control rather than in a separate card account, so a lost card does not hand anyone your funds. Freezing the card cuts off spending, and the crypto never moved. 

If Someone Is Using Your Card Online

Unauthorized charges mean your card details have leaked, often through a breached shop, a phishing page, or malware.

  • Freeze the card and request a new number
  • Report each unauthorized payment to the issuer and ask about dispute options
  • Change the password on your card app and turn on two-factor authentication
  • Scan your devices for malware, and remove browser extensions you do not recognize

Card-network payments sometimes have dispute processes, but support varies widely between crypto card providers. Report quickly, because most dispute windows are short.

If Your Account or Wallet Is Hacked

This is the serious scenario, and it needs a different response.

If your card app login was compromised, change the password immediately, revoke all active sessions, and reset two-factor authentication from a device you trust. Then contact support to lock the account while you investigate.

If your wallet seed phrase or private key was exposed, act as if the wallet is already lost. Create a brand-new wallet with a new seed phrase on a clean device, and move any remaining funds into it right away. Then reconnect your card to the new wallet. Do not try to “secure” the old wallet. Once a seed phrase leaks, that wallet can never be trusted again.

Beware of Recovery Scams

Right after a theft is when the second scam usually arrives. People who post about lost crypto online are quickly targeted by “recovery experts” promising to trace and return stolen funds for an upfront fee. They cannot. The FTC’s guide on what to know about cryptocurrency and scams notes that crypto payments typically cannot be reversed, and that anyone guaranteeing to recover your money is a red flag.

Report real theft to your card provider, the police, and the FTC or your country’s equivalent. Never pay someone who contacts you offering to get your crypto back.

How to Prevent It Happening Again

A few habits make a big difference:

  • Turn on two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, not SMS
  • Never store your seed phrase in photos, notes apps, or cloud storage
  • Set spending limits and transaction alerts in your card app
  • Use the virtual card for online shopping and keep the physical card for in-person payments
  • Keep most of your crypto in a separate wallet from your spending balance

If you are still deciding which card to use, it helps to start by comparing the top crypto cards on security features as well as fees and rewards. Instant freeze controls, real-time alerts, and self-custody spending are worth as much as a higher cashback rate on the day something goes wrong.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can someone steal my crypto with just my card?

Usually not. A physical card or its number can be used for card payments within its limits, but it does not give access to your wallet. Your seed phrase and app login are the real keys to your funds.

Can I get my money back after an unauthorized crypto card payment?

Sometimes. Card-network payments may be eligible for a dispute, depending on your provider’s policy. Report the charge immediately, since dispute windows are often short.

Should I freeze or cancel my card?

Freeze it first. Freezing is instant and reversible if the card turns up. Cancel and replace it once you confirm it is truly lost or that the details were stolen, and update any subscriptions linked to the old number.

Is it safe to use a recovery service for stolen crypto?

No. Services that promise to recover stolen crypto for an upfront fee are almost always scams. Report the theft to your provider and the authorities instead.

title: SAT Japan Adds USDT and USDC Payments With Dollar Settlement Through Triple-A
summary: SAT Japan’s Triple-A partnership lets eligible overseas vehicle buyers pay in stablecoins while the exporter receives US dollars.
content:
TL;DR

  • The vehicle-export payment partnership was announced October 29.
  • Eligible buyers can use USDT or USDC among supported methods.
  • Triple-A handles conversion and settlement into US dollars.

Japanese vehicle exporter SAT Japan has added a stablecoin payment route through Triple-A, targeting the cross-border transfers involved in buying a car from overseas. The October 29 announcement says eligible customers can use USDT and USDC while the exporter receives settlement in US dollars.

The arrangement puts the payment processor between the buyer’s digital asset and the seller’s preferred currency. SAT Japan does not need to hold or manage the stablecoins itself, according to the companies.

A high-value purchase tests payment certainty

A vehicle purchase involves more than clicking a checkout button. The seller needs to connect a substantial incoming payment to a specific vehicle and buyer, while the customer wants confidence that the transfer has arrived before shipping arrangements proceed.

Cross-border banking can add uncertainty about fees, intermediary deductions and processing times. A stablecoin route offers a different way to move value, but its commercial usefulness depends on the clarity of the complete transaction.

The buyer needs to know which asset and network are accepted, how long a quoted amount remains valid and when the seller will treat the invoice as paid. A transfer that reaches the wrong address or uses an unsupported network is not rescued by the fact that the token is designed to track a dollar.

The merchant keeps a familiar settlement currency

Receiving dollars allows the exporter to separate customer payment choice from the currency it uses for accounting and operations. That is a different proposition from a business deciding to accumulate cryptocurrency on its balance sheet.

The processor’s role is central to that separation. It must recognize the payment, carry out the required checks and deliver the agreed settlement. The blockchain leg can be rapid while the overall process still includes compliance and banking steps.

This makes the service closer to an alternative payment rail than a bet on token prices. The seller’s objective is to receive a usable, reconciled payment for a vehicle. The buyer’s objective is to complete the purchase using money they can access.

The car contract still matters

Changing the payment method does not establish the condition of a vehicle, its shipping timetable or whether it meets the rules in the destination country. Those remain parts of the purchase agreement and import process.

A payment confirmation can prove that funds moved, but it cannot by itself prove that the promised goods were delivered. Buyers and sellers still need clear documentation identifying the vehicle, the agreed price and the responsibilities around transport and cancellation.

Refund handling is another practical question. If a purchase cannot proceed, the parties need to know whether a refund will be made in bank money or a digital asset, how any conversion is priced and who bears the associated charges. Those details should be understandable before a high-value transfer is sent.

Adoption will show up in completed purchases

The most revealing metrics would be the number of customers choosing the new option, the time to confirmed settlement and the total cost compared with the alternatives available to those same buyers.

Geography will matter. A method that improves a particular corridor may offer little advantage where bank transfers are already cheap and predictable. Eligibility and local access also determine whether the option is genuinely convenient for an overseas customer.

SAT Japan and Triple-A have identified a plausible use case for stablecoins: moving substantial payments across borders while allowing a conventional merchant to settle in a familiar currency. The test is whether the integration reduces uncertainty in actual purchases, including exceptions and refunds, rather than simply adding another logo to the payment page.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: South Korea urges exchanges to boost cold storage after Binance hack
summary: South Korean crypto exchanges are already required to hold at least 80% of customer crypto in cold wallets, but the regulator is urging more.
content:
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has urged domestic crypto exchanges to increase the proportion of assets held in cold wallets after the $6.3 billion attack on Binance last week. 

In a statement Monday, the FSC said it held an emergency meeting with the Financial Supervisory Service, the Financial Security Institute, the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance (DAXA) and major crypto service providers to review the impact of the Binance hack on South Korea’s crypto market and review exchanges’ security measures. 

The FSC said it reviewed exchanges’ IT access controls, wallet withdrawal approval and signing procedures, and administrator privileges. It also urged providers to increase the proportion of assets held in offline cold wallets.

Attackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance’s internet-connected hot wallets last week, moving most of the funds in about 20 minutes, according to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. Binance has said the vast majority of users’ assets are held in cold storage.

South Korean law already requires exchanges to hold at least 80% of users’ crypto assets in cold storage, though cold wallet holdings vary considerably among South Korea’s major exchanges. 

At the end of September, Upbit’s cold wallet ratio stood at 99.17%, followed by Bithumb at 94.76% and Coinone at 85%, according to Financial Supervisory Service data cited by local media. Digital X, formerly Korbit, and GOPAX reported ratios of 82.79% and 80.54%, respectively.

Related: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US

The FSC also urged providers to continuously monitor deposits and withdrawals, secure additional incident response personnel and promptly report and share information about unusual access attempts.

Operators were also asked to set aside additional reserves and implement other security measures that could be introduced immediately to prevent similar breaches. The regulator said it would continue working with relevant agencies and the industry to prevent further attacks and limit potential damage.

Cointelegraph reached out to Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Digital X and GOPAX for comment.

The FSC’s warning comes as the Bank of Korea separately surveys 18 banks and 13 brokerages about their exposure to crypto-related risks, including major exchange hacks and prolonged market downturns. The central bank’s review began before the Binance attack.

title: XRP Adds Nearly 8,000 New Wallets in a Day Following $6 Billion Binance Hack
summary: XRP recorded one of its strongest days for new wallet creation this year after the Binance hack, according to Santiment. The increase contrasted with subdued prices, as the analytics firm suggested a possible shift toward self-custody. XRP Wallet Growth Accelerates Despite Price Pressure Santiment r...
content:
1. News
  2. Market Updates
  3. XRP Adds Nearly 8,000 New Wallets in a Day Following $6 Billion Binance Hack

Published:Nov 2, 2026, 8:10 PM EST

XRP recorded one of its strongest days for new wallet creation this year after the Binance hack, according to Santiment. The increase contrasted with subdued prices, as the analytics firm suggested a possible shift toward self-custody.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 2, 2026, 8:10 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Nov. 1 brought 7,934 new XRP wallets, the sixth-highest daily total of 2026.
  • Santiment identified $1.30 as a level to confirm stronger price momentum.
  • Wallet growth above 4,000 daily plus a $1.30 reclaim would make XRP’s setup more constructive.

XRP Wallet Growth Accelerates Despite Price Pressure

Santiment reported on Nov. 2 that 7,934 new XRP wallets were created the preceding day, marking the sixth-highest daily total of 2026. The analytics firm’s assessment of XRP network growth, shared on X, highlighted the unusually strong Sunday activity while the cryptocurrency traded near $1.25.

“XRP network growth is accelerating fast,” Santiment stated. The firm connected the timing to the aftermath of the Binance breach, while qualifying the potential relationship. Santiment added:

“The surge follows a busy week for XRP and came just after the Binance hack, which may have pushed more users toward self-custody and fresh wallets.”

The wallet count measures new addresses rather than establishing how many distinct people joined the network.

A move toward self-custody of crypto assets would place control of private keys with holders rather than an exchange. That distinction underpins Santiment’s suggestion that the breach may have pushed users toward self-custody. Creating a separate wallet can reflect a change in custody arrangements as well as participation by a new user.

Binance Breach Forms Backdrop to Network Increase

The security incident directly involved XRP. Investigators found that five Binance wallets transferred 233.46 million XRP to an attacker-controlled address in approximately four minutes on Oct. 29. Each sending wallet retained only its minimum balance, according to transaction tracing cited in the findings.

Customer backing subsequently became a central part of the exchange’s response. Binance stated on Oct. 31 that XRP and nine other cryptocurrencies were fully backed, as it replaced stolen assets using company resources. That assurance concerned reserves supporting customer balances, a separate issue from customers’ ability to withdraw during the suspension.

The exchange’s phased withdrawal recovery plan scheduled an initial reopening window for Nov. 1, with XRP among the listed networks. Binance also reported that it had covered approximately 95% of the affected amount. Less liquid tokens accounted for the remaining shortfall, and the company pledged to bear the financial impact.

Santiment Identifies Conditions for Stronger XRP Momentum

Santiment identified $1.25 as the immediate pivot and $1.30 as the first level that would confirm stronger price momentum. Its outlook also depended on sustained wallet creation. The firm detailed:

“If new-wallet growth stays above roughly 4K per day while XRP reclaims $1.30, the setup becomes more constructive. A drop below $1.20 alongside network growth falling back under 3K would weaken that signal.”

Separately, the attacker moved the stolen XRP into six fresh wallets on Nov. 2, after the assets had remained largely untouched for roughly 80 hours. Those transfers occurred after the daily period highlighted by Santiment. Nine large payments between 3:52 and 4 a.m. UTC redistributed approximately 233.45 million XRP. As of writing, XRP is trading at $1.25.

About the author

WRITTEN BYKevin Helms

Kevin Helms is a cryptocurrency journalist specializing in Bitcoin, blockchain regulation, and global digital asset markets.

title: Ripple and Water.org Expand Stablecoin Work as Aid Payments Move Faster
summary: Ripple and Water.org are expanding payments, RLUSD and custody work, with the central test being how efficiently funding reaches local lenders.
content:
TL;DR

  • Ripple announced an expanded Water.org partnership in late October.
  • The work includes payments, stablecoin settlement and digital-asset management.
  • Funding delivery and household outcomes require separate measurement.

Ripple and Water.org are expanding a partnership that applies payment and stablecoin infrastructure to water and sanitation financing. Ripple’s late-October announcement describes wider use of Ripple Payments, RLUSD and wallet services across the nonprofit’s operations.

The company reports that earlier work moved more than $3.2 million across four markets, with same-day settlement in Mexico and Brazil replacing waits of two to three days. Those are partner-reported operational results, not an independent measure of every programme outcome.

The financing model explains the payment need

Water.org’s WaterCredit programme works with local financial institutions to make small loans for household water and sanitation improvements. Its role includes supporting partners with resources and expertise, while those institutions provide the financing.

That model makes the movement of capital an important operational link. Money may originate in one country, pass through an international funding arrangement and ultimately support a local loan used to install a tap, toilet or other improvement.

Speed in one part of that chain can help, particularly when it reduces idle balances or uncertainty over when funds will arrive. It cannot substitute for sound lending, reliable local contractors or a household’s ability to use the completed infrastructure.

Payment savings need to survive the full journey

A cross-border transfer can involve several forms of cost: bank charges, currency conversion, the time staff spend reconciling records and the cash held while a payment is pending. A change in infrastructure may improve some of those elements without changing all of them.

The useful comparison is therefore the amount and timing of usable money at the destination. A token arriving quickly is not the same as a local lender having the currency and information needed to disburse a loan.

For example, a settlement message that arrives over a weekend may still require a local conversion or approval process. Measuring that whole sequence would show whether continuous digital settlement translates into a practical advantage for the programme.

Stablecoin settlement changes treasury work

Adding a stablecoin gives an organization another way to hold and transfer a claim denominated in dollars. It also creates tasks around access permissions, reconciliation and the conditions for converting the balance into another form of money.

A nonprofit’s finance team needs to connect those balances to grants, programme budgets and expenditure records. The technology is most useful when it fits that discipline, rather than requiring the organization to maintain a separate set of unexplained onchain transactions.

Custody and wallet services can form part of that operating model. The important question is who is allowed to move funds and how the organization checks that an instruction matches an approved purpose. Faster settlement increases the value of getting those controls right before execution.

Operational success and social impact are different measures

Payment completion times and processing costs show whether the financial infrastructure works more efficiently. Household access to safe water and sanitation shows whether the wider programme achieves its purpose. Both are relevant, but one should not be used as an automatic proxy for the other.

A credible expansion would report the relationship between the two: whether lower costs leave more funding available, whether quicker transfers improve loan availability and whether local delivery remains reliable as the programme grows.

For crypto, this is an adoption story with a concrete use for moving money, rather than a claim that a token’s price must benefit. The partnership gives Ripple and Water.org a setting in which payment infrastructure can be assessed against a practical objective. The strongest results will be those that trace an operational improvement through to the people the financing is intended to reach.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Binance Hack Funds Spread Across 12,000 Wallets in Under Four Days
summary: Funds stolen from Binance passed through approximately 12,000 wallets in under four days, Elliptic found. The operation spanned 11 blockchains, while the firm assessed that only a negligible amount had likely been cashed out. Thousands of Wallets Expand the Laundering Trail Crypto assets stolen from...
content:
Funds stolen from Binance passed through approximately 12,000 wallets in under four days, Elliptic found. The operation spanned 11 blockchains, while the firm assessed that only a negligible amount had likely been cashed out.

Key Takeaways

  • The operation used roughly one new wallet every 25 seconds.
  • Elliptic found conventional automation rather than evidence of AI agents.
  • About $3.24 billion remained in theft-linked addresses as of Nov. 2.

Thousands of Wallets Expand the Laundering Trail

Crypto assets stolen from Binance moved through approximately 12,000 wallets across 11 blockchains in under four days, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported on Nov. 2. Its analysis of the 12,000-wallet laundering operation tracked more than 40,000 transactions following the Oct. 29 theft of $6.43 billion. Elliptic stated:

“The laundering is highly complex and clearly automated.”

Chainalysis had identified suspected automated laundering patterns on Oct. 30, observing repeated transfers between addresses and returns to wallets used earlier. Many receiving addresses obtained exactly 1 TRX, Tron’s native cryptocurrency, for transaction fees before accepting and forwarding larger balances. That recurring sequence suggested software was redistributing the proceeds.

The theft itself involved additional entry points and bypassed approval controls, Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said in a video shared Oct. 30. He described an investigation extending beyond an initially suspected compromised laptop. A self-destruct mechanism also destroyed attack tools and traces, complicating the exchange’s investigation.

Automated Transfers Lead Into Vaults and Bitcoin Mixing

Elliptic identified fixed timing, set amounts, and blind retries. Those patterns pointed to conventional software scripts. The firm found no evidence that artificial intelligence software was making decisions about the transfers.

The attacker also used lending vaults, protocol contracts that accept deposits and process withdrawals, to deposit from one address and withdraw to others without a direct transfer between them. Bitcoin mixing began Nov. 1, with approximately 28 BTC, worth $2.2 million, passing through 18 coinjoins by early Nov. 2. Coinjoins combine multiple users’ bitcoin inputs and outputs in shared transactions, making individual movements harder to trace.

Attempts to move assets intersected with Thorchain’s emergency swapping pause. The protocol, which enables cryptocurrency swaps across blockchains, activated safeguards after an accounting discrepancy involving 10 ETH on Oct. 31. Chainalysis said the malfunction inadvertently delayed laundering connected to the Binance theft.

Exchanges Face Pressure to Block Cash-Out Attempts

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the Binance theft to North Korea on Oct. 31, identifying the activity as Tradertraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group. Working with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, it observed conversions primarily into ether. Authorities urged exchanges, infrastructure operators, and decentralized finance services to block transactions involving the listed addresses.

Intervention depends partly on the assets involved. Stablecoin freeze and blacklist controls allow issuers to prevent designated addresses from transferring tokens even when holders control their wallet keys. Exchanges can separately restrict deposits or freeze accounts, providing another intervention point for cryptocurrencies without issuer-controlled freezes.

Elliptic’s chart traces the stolen assets from their original form on Oct. 29 through swaps, freezes, and remaining holdings as of Nov. 2. It shows $2.85 billion frozen, while the attacker retained approximately $1.43 billion in bitcoin across 40 addresses and $1.37 billion in ether across 857 addresses. A separate $16 million flowed into addresses containing Bitget-exploit proceeds, indicating that some funds from the two thefts were combined.

Changing one cryptocurrency into another does not itself establish a cash-out. Elliptic estimated that approximately $3.24 billion remained in theft-linked addresses at that observation time, mostly in ether and bitcoin. It expected eventual cash-out attempts through over-the-counter brokers over several months.

title: Taurus Adds Stellar Smart-Contract Assets to Institutional Custody and Issuance
summary: Taurus says its Stellar integration now supports smart-contract assets, extending the tasks institutions can perform through existing custody controls.
content:
TL;DR

  • Taurus announced live smart-contract asset support on October 29.
  • The extension covers its custody and tokenization platforms.
  • Institutional adoption depends on controls around the full asset lifecycle.

Taurus has expanded its Stellar integration to support smart-contract-based assets, giving institutional clients a broader set of custody and issuance functions. The company said on October 29 that the capabilities are live through Taurus-PROTECT and Taurus-CAPITAL.

The official announcement describes an extension of existing Stellar support rather than a newly announced fund or security. The change matters because institutions need more than a place to store a token once it has been created.

Custody includes authority over transactions

Safekeeping is often described as protecting private keys. For an institution, a useful custody system must also govern what those keys are allowed to authorize, who can request an action and which approvals are needed before it proceeds.

A simple transfer and a smart-contract interaction can carry different consequences. An instruction may change an allowance, invoke a contract function or alter how an asset can be handled. The approving person needs enough information to understand that consequence before a signature is produced.

This creates a practical reason to integrate smart-contract support into the tools an institution already uses. A separate experimental interface may be technically capable of sending an instruction while sitting outside the organization’s normal operating controls.

Issuance is the beginning of an asset’s life

Creating a tokenized instrument requires decisions about the rights it represents and the actions permitted after issuance. Depending on the instrument, those may include transfers, subscriptions, redemptions or changes governed by the issuer’s rules.

Taurus says the release supports several Stellar token models, including structures intended for regulated assets. That flexibility can help an institution match its technical implementation to the instrument it wants to offer, rather than treating every token as economically identical.

It also raises an integration question: can the legal and operational records remain consistent with the contract state? A token should not appear transferable in an application when the issuer’s rules prohibit the intended recipient from holding it.

Common infrastructure can reduce duplicate work

A financial firm considering another blockchain faces costs beyond deploying a contract. Staff need familiar approval processes, finance teams need reports and operations teams need a procedure for handling failed instructions.

Reusing an established custody and issuance interface may reduce the number of new systems those teams must learn. It can also make oversight more consistent across networks, provided the interface still exposes the differences that matter.

For example, an operations dashboard should not imply that two assets have identical settlement behaviour simply because they appear in neighbouring rows. Network-specific requirements, contract permissions and servicing obligations need to remain visible where they affect decisions.

Live support needs a live business use

The release establishes that clients have more infrastructure options on Stellar. The next evidence of adoption would be institutions using those capabilities for named instruments with clearly explained ownership and transfer arrangements.

There is a difference between supporting a contract standard and completing a reliable asset-servicing process. A production service must handle routine transactions, unusual requests and the reconciliation that follows. Its value lies in reducing the effort required to do those jobs correctly.

For Stellar, the potential benefit is a wider route for institutional asset activity. For Taurus clients, it is the ability to consider another network without rebuilding every surrounding control. Neither outcome should be measured simply by the number of token standards listed in a release.

The more revealing test is whether an issuer can take an asset from creation through ongoing management and eventual redemption using a coherent set of records. Taurus’s announcement expands the available toolkit for that work; actual products and operating results will show how effectively it is used.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US
summary: Pyongyang has pushed back against the FBI’s attribution of the Binance attack, with Kim Yo Jong calling the US allegations politically motivated.
content:
Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denied North Korea’s involvement in the $6.3 billion Binance hack and appeared to suggest, without evidence, that the US could have been behind the theft.

In a statement released via the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) on Tuesday, Kim rejected the FBI’s attribution of the attack to a North Korean-backed hacking group.

“The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a ‘cyber criminal state’, claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in the incident,” said Kim. “But the US assertion is an absurd rhetoric and nothing new.”

She described the allegations as a political provocation intended to damage North Korea’s international standing. The FBI also blamed North Korea for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, an accusation Kim also rejected on Tuesday.

“This is not the first time that the U.S. has attempted to spread misunderstanding of the DPRK in the international community, blindly linking the DPRK with the ‘cyber crime’ incidents whenever they occur on an international scale,” said Kim.

Kim casts suspicion on US over Binance hack

Kim also pointed the finger at the US for involvement in the hack.

“If it carefully examines who will get the large amount of the so-called stolen cryptocurrency when the latter is retrieved, it may get a clue about who is behind the hacking incident,” she said.

The statement provided no evidence connecting Washington to the attack. Cointelegraph reached out to the FBI for comment.

Investigators cite links to earlier North Korean hacks

Last week, blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs attributed the Binance attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group with high confidence, citing onchain and offchain intelligence. Other investigators, including Chainalysis and ZachXBT, also linked the theft to North Korean hackers.

TRM Labs pointed to similarities with previous North Korean attacks, including advance preparation, the use of Tornado Cash to fund attacker wallets and the coordinated execution of previously obtained transaction signatures. However, it said the laundering activity differed from the pattern following the Bybit hack.

Onchain investigator ZachXBT also identified a connection between the Binance and Bitget hacks, saying stolen funds from both incidents were commingled at the same address after passing through THORChain. During early investigation into the hack, Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said preliminary findings linked IP addresses to VPN services used “by a certain DPRK group.”

Related: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack

title: Airtm and BVNK Plan Wallet Payments for Merchants in Emerging Markets
summary: Airtm’s planned BVNK integration connects wallet balances to merchant payments, testing whether digital dollars can move beyond storage and transfers.
content:
TL;DR

  • The partnership was announced on October 29.
  • Airtm Connect links wallets with participating BVNK retailers.
  • The consumer test is a dependable end-to-end payment experience.

Airtm and BVNK have announced an integration intended to let users spend wallet funds with participating retailers, extending digital-dollar services beyond receiving and holding money. The October 29 joint announcement links Airtm Connect with BVNK’s stablecoin-payment infrastructure and says the integration will use Stellar.

The commercial objective is straightforward: a balance becomes more useful if its owner can spend it without repeatedly moving through disconnected services. Delivering that convenience requires the entire payment process to work, including the steps outside the blockchain.

A wallet balance needs an exit into commerce

A customer who receives digital dollars may still need to pay merchants using a different system. Each conversion or transfer can introduce a fee, a delay and another opportunity to select the wrong details.

Connecting a wallet directly to a merchant payment flow could remove some of that handling. The user would begin with the balance they already possess, rather than first preparing money in a separate account solely for the purchase.

The improvement depends on whether the customer can understand the final cost before confirming. A low network fee is only one element. Exchange rates, payment-provider charges and any conversion into the merchant’s chosen settlement currency also determine what the purchase actually costs.

Funding and spending must work together

A payment option is difficult to use regularly if adding money to the wallet is unreliable. Conversely, convenient funding has limited value if the customer cannot use the resulting balance where they shop.

The partnership combines providers working at different parts of that chain. The implication is a chance to make funding, wallet access and merchant acceptance feel like one service, even when multiple organizations perform the underlying work.

Consider someone paid by an overseas customer who then purchases a subscription. A coherent flow should preserve enough information to show the incoming payment, the available balance, the purchase and any refund. If the customer must reconstruct those records across several interfaces, some of the convenience has been lost.

Payment status is a commercial fact

A successful network transaction and a completed retail order are related, but they are not identical. The merchant needs to know that the transfer corresponds to a valid order and meets its settlement requirements before delivering the product.

That creates several possible intermediate states. A customer may approve a payment after the original quote expires. A merchant may cancel an order while a transfer is processing. A service may need to reverse the commercial transaction even though the blockchain transfer itself cannot simply be deleted.

These are normal payment-system problems rather than reasons to dismiss the model. The quality of an integration shows in how consistently it handles them, especially for users who cannot afford to wait through a lengthy support process to recover a modest balance.

Measuring access rather than potential reach

The announcement establishes a planned route to participating retailers. It does not imply that every merchant connected to a broader financial network will immediately accept an Airtm wallet payment.

Practical evidence would include which countries and merchants are enabled, the available funding methods and the time between payment approval and a usable settlement balance. Successful repeat purchases would say more about adoption than the number of people who could theoretically access the service.

For stablecoin markets, this is a useful test of whether digital-dollar infrastructure can support ordinary spending without adding complexity for the customer. Airtm and BVNK have described the connection they want to build. Its value will come from how well funding, checkout and after-sales support fit together once people use it.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Crypto Bank Custodia Urges Supreme Court to End ‘Tyranny’ of Federal Reserve
summary: Custodia Bank has filed a reply brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to review a 10th Circuit decision that allowed regional Federal Reserve banks to deny master accounts to eligible institutions. Supreme Court Appeal Crypto-focused Custodia Bank has issued a renewed plea to the U.S. Supreme Court to...
content:
Custodia Bank has filed a reply brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to review a 10th Circuit decision that allowed regional Federal Reserve banks to deny master accounts to eligible institutions.

Key Takeaways

  • Custodia Bank filed a reply brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to review a 10th Circuit ruling.
  • Regional Federal Reserve banks gained discretion to block eligible crypto institutions from master accounts.
  • If left intact, the Monetary Control Act of 1980 dispute could reshape dual banking system power.

Supreme Court Appeal

Crypto-focused Custodia Bank has issued a renewed plea to the U.S. Supreme Court to take up its battle against the Federal Reserve, per a report from Law360, arguing that only the high court can “put an end to the Fed’s tyranny over financial innovation.”

In a reply brief filed in support of its petition for a writ of certiorari, the bank asked the justices to review a decision from the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. The appellate ruling upheld the Federal Reserve System’s discretion to deny master accounts to otherwise statutorily eligible depository institutions.

Custodia contends that the appellate court’s decision improperly equips unappointed regional bank presidents with authority to block “disfavored” banking institutions from accessing core payment rails. Reemphasizing the broader legal and economic stakes, Custodia described the consequences of the decision as “profound.”

The bank stressed that the statutory questions presented have generated “deep disagreement among a range of respected jurists, with thoughtful opinions on both sides of the issue,” making immediate Supreme Court intervention necessary despite the absence of a direct circuit split.

If left intact, the lower court’s ruling threatens to undermine the nation’s traditional dual banking system and severely “cripple” the ability of individual states to foster financial innovation.

“The decision vests extensive regulatory authority in unappointed bureaucrats, creating a judicially sanctioned safe harbor for a newly constituted fourth branch of government,” Custodia asserted in its brief. “The practical stakes are likewise staggering. The Fed’s asserted discretion to deprive depository institutions of master-account access hangs over every bank like a sword of Damocles.”

Statutory Dispute Over the Monetary Control Act

At the center of the dispute is the interpretation of the Monetary Control Act of 1980. Custodia argues that the statute explicitly mandates that the Federal Reserve “shall” make its payment services available to eligible banks, leaving no statutory leeway for regional Reserve Banks to enact policy-based rejections. The Federal Reserve has argued that the absence of the word “all” prior to “nonmember depository institutions” means payment services are only required to be made available to institutions “as a class.”

However, Custodia pushed back against that reading in its reply, pointing out that the Monetary Control Act incorporates a definition of “depository institution” covering “any bank which is eligible” to apply for Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insurance. Consequently, Custodia argues, the text requires Reserve Banks to open payment services to “any” legally eligible nonmember bank.

Custodia initially sued the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City in 2022, alleging undue delay in processing its master account application. It renewed the litigation in early 2023 after the Fed formally rejected the application, citing concerns that Custodia’s risk management framework was inadequate for managing cryptocurrency risks.

A federal judge in Wyoming ruled in favor of the Fed, a decision later affirmed by a panel of the 10th Circuit. However, the appellate panel was split. Circuit Judge Timothy M. Tymkovich wrote a dissent, warning that the majority decision granted the Fed “unreviewable discretion” to deny master accounts and effectively handed central bankers a veto over state chartering authorities.

Since filing its cert petition, Custodia’s position has drawn backing from prominent lawmakers and industry advocacy groups. Former U.S. Sen. Pat Toomey joined U.S. Sen. Cynthia Lummis in an amicus brief. The lawmakers argued that the 10th Circuit misconstrued congressional disclosure mandates as a structural grant of agency discretion.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto: Mercado Bitcoin halted deposits and withdrawals after a hack reportedly drained more than $46 million from its wallets. Binance’s emergency Bitcoin reserves fell to roughly half their pre-hack level as the exchange moved to cover $6.3 billion in losses from an attack the FBI attributed to North Korea.

Mercado Bitcoin wallets show post-hack transfers after $46M theft

Mercado Bitcoin, one of Brazil’s largest cryptocurrency exchanges, confirmed a security incident on Monday that blockchain analysts estimated drained more than $46 million from its wallets. Despite the company’s announcement that it had suspended deposits and withdrawals, addresses associated with the incident continued to receive funds for hours afterward.

Senior security engineer at Certik, Dickson Wu, published an initial post-mortem of the incident, saying the attackers “picked at eight small chains for four hours,” including Base, Optimism and Arbitrum. The attack then moved to the company’s main hot wallets before transferring tiny amounts of Ether (ETH) from 27,160 different addresses.

“So whoever did this can also move money out of MB’s customer deposit addresses,” he wrote.

Security firms have stated the hack was carried out through standard transfers rather than a smart contract exploit. 

A spokesperson for Mercado Bitcoin told Cointelegraph that customers had suffered no losses and no data had been leaked, but the company did not respond to requests for comment on the continued transfers. A data breach could also trigger notification requirements to Brazil’s data protection authority.

The hack has not yet been attributed to an organized group and remains under investigation.

Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof

Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack.

The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).

As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer.

Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions.

The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses.

FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack

The FBI said that the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of about $6.3 billion in digital assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance on Thursday.

The FBI said on Saturday in a news release that it refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as “TraderTraitor,” which it has most recently observed converting stolen assets mostly into Ether (ETH). 

It expects these assets to be further converted, using DeFi and instant swap services, as the hackers move to more advanced laundering stages.

The FBI urged private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets. A full list of addresses is provided on the news release.

title: New Jersey drops Coinbase staking order ahead of crypto’s midterm test
summary: New Jersey lifted its staking ban and dropped a $5 million penalty, clearing the way for Coinbase to restore staking access for users in the US state.
content:
New Jersey’s securities regulator has rescinded its 2023 cease-and-desist order against Coinbase’s staking service, lifting a ban that stopped residents staking new funds on the exchange for over three years.

The Oct. 30 notice, signed by Acting Bureau Chief Keith A. Alt, withdrew the order and its $5 million penalty without prejudice and without a ruling on the merits. The wording leaves the Bureau of Securities free to bring a fresh enforcement action against Coinbase in the future. 

Coinbase disclosed the move in its third-quarter filing, stating the regulator informed the company on Oct. 29 of its plan to rescind. CEO Brian Armstrong said New Jersey users would regain staking access “very soon”. 

California, Maryland, Wisconsin and Washington are still pursuing enforcement actions against the exchange with cases against the its staking services. 

Staking involves committing cryptocurrency to help validate transactions and secure a blockchain in exchange for rewards. Companies like Coinbase handle the process for customers and take a share of the rewards as a fee.

The last holdouts

California led the ten-state task force behind the 2023 actions, which covered more than 600,000 accounts held by Californians.

Like New Jersey, California and Wisconsin and Maryland banned Coinbase from new staking while their cases ran. Washington’s regulator allows staking but the ongoing case seeks to impose a $4 million fine on the exchange.

Coinbase estimates that California users have missed out on over $89 million in staking rewards since 2023, against more than $15 million in New Jersey.

Crypto’s federal fix stalls before the vote

The decision came ahead of the Nov. 3 US midterm elections, with prediction markets favoring Democrats to win the Senate control. A Democratic majority would put Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a prominent crypto critic, in line to chair the Senate Banking Committee, while Sen. Cynthia Lummis, a leading Republican advocate for the industry, is set to retire in January 2027.

New Jersey’s reversal came under Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill, who voted for both the CLARITY and GENIUS bills as a House member. The state’s Democratic senator, Cory Booker, also helped negotiate market structure legislation, though he opposed advancing CLARITY in September.

The industry has sought to build support across party lines ahead of the midterms. Fairshake and its affiliated super PACs are backing 19 Republicans and 14 Democrats in House races, while New Jersey’s Josh Gottheimer has also received crypto-industry support. The number of members of Congress with an A rating from advocacy group Stand With Crypto has risen to 332, up from 96 when the group launched in 2023, according to Reuters.

title: WalletConnect Adds Stellar Payments as Bermuda Ticketing Rollout Targets 2027
summary: WalletConnect Pay now supports Stellar, while its planned Bermuda ticketing integration is expected in the second quarter of 2027.
content:
TL;DR

  • WalletConnect announced expanded Stellar support on October 29.
  • LOBSTR is described as the first live wallet for Stellar payments.
  • The PTIX merchant rollout is expected in Q2 2027.

WalletConnect is expanding payment access on Stellar while preparing a separate merchant rollout in Bermuda. Its October 29 announcement says WalletConnect Pay supports the network, with LOBSTR as the first live Stellar wallet.

The Bermuda initiative, developed with Penrose Partners, begins with ticketing platform Premier Tickets, or PTIX. That integration is expected in the second quarter of 2027, so wallet support available now should be distinguished from the planned merchant launch.

Connecting a wallet is only the first step

A payment interface needs to identify both the customer’s wallet and the transaction the merchant expects. Those tasks sound simple until an order expires, a customer changes devices or a transfer arrives after the checkout page has been closed.

For ticketing, the sequence is particularly important. The buyer wants confirmation that a seat has been secured; the organizer needs confidence that payment belongs to the correct order. A blockchain transaction hash does not, by itself, contain every detail of that commercial relationship.

A useful integration must connect payment status to inventory and customer support. Otherwise, a fast transfer can still create a slow service experience when the ticketing system cannot confidently match the money to the purchase.

Direct settlement changes the platform’s role

The proposed PTIX arrangement sends customer funds to the event organizer’s wallet without the ticketing platform holding them. That design changes where money sits between the moment a customer pays and the moment the organizer can use it.

It can reduce the need for the platform to collect and subsequently distribute balances. It also requires careful handling of refunds, disputed orders and changes to an event. Those obligations do not disappear because the transfer takes a more direct route.

A cancelled concert offers a straightforward example. Returning a payment requires identifying the right recipient, confirming the amount and deciding which party is responsible for making the transfer. A well-designed service should make that process comprehensible to a customer who has no interest in the underlying network.

Merchant adoption needs familiar accounting

For an organizer, receiving a digital asset is useful only if it fits the business’s finances. The organizer needs to know how much usable value it has received, what costs apply and how the balance will pay suppliers or other expenses.

Some businesses may want to retain a token; others may prefer conversion into bank money. Those choices affect reconciliation and liquidity planning. The availability of a wallet connection does not establish that every merchant will make the same decision.

Payment records also need to remain useful after the event. A business must be able to connect sales, refunds and settlement to its own accounts. The more the system can handle these ordinary tasks predictably, the less specialist knowledge a merchant needs to accept the payment method.

The rollout provides a concrete adoption test

The announced timeline gives observers a clear milestone: a functioning ticket purchase from a supported wallet, with a merchant receiving the expected funds and a buyer receiving the correct ticket. That is a more useful measure than the theoretical reach of a wallet network.

After launch, repeat use and the rate of failed or abandoned payments would help assess whether the option solves a real customer problem. Lower processing costs would matter if they survive the full journey, including conversion and support.

WalletConnect’s Stellar expansion opens a technical route, while the Bermuda project attempts to give that route a regular commercial purpose. The two developments fit together, but their different launch stages need to remain clear as the integration progresses.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: AI poses greater threat to Bitcoin than quantum computing, Swan founder says
summary: The Swan Bitcoin founder warned that hackers are using large language models to exploit security flaws with just a few prompts.
content:
Artificial intelligence poses a more immediate threat to Bitcoin security than quantum computing, according to Swan Bitcoin founder Cory Klippsten, who warned that hackers are increasingly using AI to exploit vulnerabilities as crypto exchanges face a string of security breaches.

Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction, Klippsten dismissed much of the concern surrounding quantum computing as speculative, arguing that advances in large language models present a more pressing challenge as attackers use the technology to probe security weaknesses.

I think we’re finding out that the near term threat is actually AI. That it’s these LLMs in the hands of hackers going and poking through everything. And that’s where you see this over and over and over again.

The warning comes as Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals on Monday following a security incident, with researchers estimating that more than $46 million had left its wallets. Just days earlier, exchange Binance lost $6.3 billion in an Oct. 29 hack that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed to North Korean hackers.

Source: Cointelegraph

Bitcoin has time to address quantum risks

Klippsten estimated that quantum computers capable of threatening Bitcoin’s cryptography remain at least a decade away, potentially longer. He argued that the network could adopt quantum-resistant protections if the threat became credible, but said rushing to implement them now would introduce unnecessary complexity.

He warned that cryptocurrency companies cannot rely on hastily developed software when safeguarding customer assets. “You need to actually know what the hell you’re doing from a security standpoint,” he said.

Klippsten also suggested that some cryptocurrency startups and investors had used fears surrounding quantum computing to attract funding, characterizing much of the discussion as fear, uncertainty and doubt (“FUD”) rather than an imminent security concern.

title: Kalshi, Polymarket Predictors Favor Democrats to Sweep 2026 Midterms
summary: Both prediction market platforms predict Democrats will retake control of both the House and Senate in the upcoming midterm elections, although their record has been muddled by President Lula’s upset victory in Brazil’s recent runoff election. Polymarket and Kalshi Predict Democrat Sweep in Upcoming...
content:
Both prediction market platforms predict Democrats will retake control of both the House and Senate in the upcoming midterm elections, although their record has been muddled by President Lula’s upset victory in Brazil’s recent runoff election.

Key Takeaways

  • Prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi give Democrats a 74% chance of winning both the House and Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections.
  • Traditional pollsters align with the betting odds, suggesting a potential “blue wave” in the midterms.
  • The growing influence of these platforms has sparked concerns about their impact on voter behavior.

Polymarket and Kalshi Predict Democrat Sweep in Upcoming Elections

Prediction markets, which have proven to be somewhat reliable when it comes to political outcomes, are signaling a clear advantage for the Democratic Party on the eve of the upcoming midterm elections, when all 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 seats in the U.S. Senate will be contested.

Polymarket’s Balance of Power: 2026 Midterms event market, which has a volume of over $58 million, gives Democrats a 78% chance of winning control of both the House and the Senate, while only maintaining an 18% probability for Republicans to maintain a majority in the Senate.

Similarly, Kalshi, which has a dedicated portal for the midterm elections, gives Democrats 74% odds of sweeping the election in a similar event market. The contract, which has moved over $100 million in volume, only gives Republicans a 22% chance of retaining Senate control, as of this writing.

Democrats are favored by bets in relevant individual Senate races in both platforms. For example, in Texas, James Talarico has the upper hand on both platforms 74% to 76% odds of winning the seat over Republican Ken Paxton. Troy Jackson also enjoys a lead of 73% against Maine Republican Susan Collins on both platforms, while in Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed is favored by 78% on both Polymarket and Kalshi at the moment of writing.

This time, traditional pollsters are on the side of prediction markets, with CNN’s data analyst Harry Enten describing the potential outcome as a “polling earthquake.”

“Just within the last few hours, we had the equivalent of a polling earthquake, And to keep up with the weather metaphors… it tends to point to a blue wave,” said Enten on Sunday.

Prediction markets entered the political sphere with strength after accurately predicting President Trump’s victory in 2024 when some traditional pollsters gave an edge to Democrat candidate Kamala Harris. The midterm election is the biggest relevant test for these platforms since then, with Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour calling these “the first prediction-market election,” with over $1.4 billion traded in midterm-linked bets.

Nonetheless, since 2024, the accuracy of these platforms has been spotty at best, with prediction markets failing to track the upset victory of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva after giving Senator Flavio Bolsonaro the lead before the runoff election.

The influence of prediction markets on voting events is under scrutiny for the first time, with institutions like the Center for Democracy and Technology stressing that they can distort candidate decisions, impact voter behavior, and undermine confidence in election processes and outcomes.

title: Crypto investigators flag suspected $106M theft, $786K Solana bot drain
summary: A European entity may have lost $106 million from exchange accounts, while a wallet associated with a Solana arbitrage bot may have lost another $786,000.
content:
An unidentified entity in the European Union may have lost more than $106 million from accounts at multiple cryptocurrency exchanges on Sunday, according to blockchain investigator ZachXBT.

In a Monday post, ZachXBT said funds suspected to have been stolen were withdrawn in USDC and USDT before being moved through several cryptocurrencies and blockchains.

The suspected attacker swapped USDC for Ether (ETH), used instant exchange services including WellWallet and Kyrrex, and converted funds into Monero (XMR) through the swap service Wagyu.

Source: ZachXBT Telegram post

The suspected attacker remains unidentified, though ZachXBT said the movement of funds pointed away from a link to North Korea’s Lazarus Group. The affected entity and exchanges involved have not been publicly named.

ZachXBT identified 11 wallet addresses associated with the funds.

The reported theft follows the $6.3 billion Binance hack on Oct. 29, which the FBI has attributed to North Korean hackers known as “TraderTraitor,” a group linked to Lazarus. The attack was the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

Related: Binance net outflows surge to $5.8B as withdrawals resume after record hack

Wallet associated with Solana arbitrage bot may have lost $786K

A wallet associated with King, an automated trading bot on Solana, may have lost about $786,000 on Monday, according to pseudonymous blockchain monitoring account Onchain Lens.

King is an arbitrage bot, a software that automatically buys cryptocurrency in one market and sells it in another to profit from price differences. Onchain Lens told Cointelegraph the funds moved through several Solana wallets before being transferred to Ethereum using Mayan, a service for moving assets between blockchains. It said the rapid transfers suggested an attempt to conceal the funds’ origin and a possible wallet compromise.

King’s operator has not confirmed a compromise.

“Our report is based on unusual fund movements, rapid transfers and the subsequent cross-chain movement of funds, which we believe indicates an attempt to obscure their origin,” Onchain Lens told Cointelegraph. “This pattern strongly suggests a potential wallet compromise.”
