title: Hashdex Adds Jane Street to Crypto Index ETF Authorized Participants
summary: An October 30 prospectus supplement adds Jane Street Capital to Hashdex’s authorized participants, expanding its listed creation-and-redemption network.
content:
TL;DR

  • Jane Street Capital joined the ETF’s listed authorized participants.
  • The change appears in an October 30 prospectus supplement.
  • The appointment is different from an investor inflow.

Hashdex Nasdaq CME Crypto Index ETF has added Jane Street Capital to its list of authorized participants, according to an October 30 prospectus supplement. The document updates the firms able to participate in the product’s creation-and-redemption arrangements.

It is a market-structure development rather than a statement that Jane Street has made a long-term investment in the fund. That distinction matters when institutional names become attached to crypto products.

What an authorized participant does

The SEC’s investor glossary describes authorized participants as financial institutions that enter contractual arrangements to buy and redeem creation units. Their role links the supply of a fund’s shares to activity in the market where those shares trade.

Most ordinary investors transact with another market participant through a brokerage account. An authorized participant operates at a different layer, dealing with larger blocks under the product’s documented procedures. The two activities support the same product but should not be confused.

A listed participant can make the infrastructure available without committing to create shares on every trading day. The appointment establishes a relationship and a permitted function. Actual activity depends on market conditions, commercial decisions and the rules governing the fund.

Why more routes can matter

When demand for shares changes, the mechanisms for adjusting supply can influence how closely the traded price stays connected to underlying asset value. If those mechanisms are difficult or expensive to use, gaps can persist even when traders recognize them.

An additional participant may offer another route through which the market can respond. That can be useful if existing firms face their own balance-sheet constraints or operational interruptions. It does not guarantee narrower spreads, because execution also depends on the liquidity of the assets and the cost of hedging.

Consider a period when investors want to buy shares rapidly while underlying crypto markets are moving. A firm providing liquidity has to manage the price risk between the share transaction and the corresponding asset trade. Access to a creation process is necessary for some workflows, but it does not make that exposure disappear.

Trading relationships are not ownership forecasts

The Hashdex supplement also identifies an affiliation between Jane Street Capital and a crypto trading counterparty. Such disclosures help readers understand how firms involved in different parts of the process are connected.

The relevant analytical question is whether the structure can process orders reliably and on competitive terms. An institutional service relationship is not evidence that the firm expects the underlying cryptocurrencies to rise or that it will retain a directional position.

This is particularly important when reading fund-flow headlines. Net new shares, secondary-market turnover and an authorized-participant appointment describe different things. One concerns changes in product size, another concerns trading between holders, and the third concerns the operating network behind the product.

Execution data will reveal the practical effect

Useful follow-up measures include trading spreads, premiums or discounts and the consistency of creation and redemption activity. Those observations would show whether the expanded network changes the experience for investors.

They also need context. A wider spread during an unusually volatile session does not automatically establish that the fund’s structure has failed. Comparing conditions over time and against underlying-market liquidity is more informative than judging a single quote.

The October filing is a relatively small document with a meaningful operational purpose: it updates who can help connect the fund to its underlying markets. It adds a recognizable financial firm to that machinery, while leaving the investment case and future flow direction open to separate assessment.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Metaplanet Buys Back 96.4M Shares to Boost Bitcoin Per Share
summary: Metaplanet repurchased 96.4 million shares in just over two weeks, deploying about $160 million as the bitcoin treasury company shifts capital toward reducing its share count. The Tokyo-listed firm has already completed nearly half of its authorized buyback of shares while simultaneously freeing mor...
content:
Metaplanet repurchased 96.4 million shares in just over two weeks, deploying about $160 million as the bitcoin treasury company shifts capital toward reducing its share count. The Tokyo-listed firm has already completed nearly half of its authorized buyback of shares while simultaneously freeing more capital for future bitcoin purchases.

Key Takeaways

  • Metaplanet repurchased 96.4M shares for about $160M, using nearly half its authorized share count.
  • The buyback aims to lift bitcoin per share while preserving flexibility for future BTC purchases.
  • With $211.7M still available, Metaplanet can choose between buying bitcoin or its own stock.

Metaplanet Turns Its Stock Into a Capital-Allocation Trade

Metaplanet is showing that a bitcoin treasury strategy does not always mean buying more bitcoin.

Between Oct. 14 and Oct. 31, the Japanese company repurchased 96,447,400 shares for about $160 million (¥25.27 billion) through Tokyo Stock Exchange purchases. That represents roughly 7.1% of its issued shares and about 48% of the maximum 200 million shares authorized under its current program.

The full buyback permits up to $380 million (¥60 billion) of purchases through Oct. 13, 2027.

The move reflects a more flexible approach to increasing bitcoin exposure for shareholders.

Metaplanet CEO Simon Gerovich said the firm will continue allocating capital “with discipline, taking into account share price, mNAV, and market conditions.”

The objective, he said, remains “maximizing bitcoin per share.”

That distinction matters. When a bitcoin treasury company trades below what management considers an attractive valuation, repurchasing shares can reduce the denominator used to calculate bitcoin per share without requiring another BTC purchase.

The strategy gives Metaplanet another lever beyond issuing securities and accumulating crypto.

Nearly Half the Share Authorization Is Already Used

The pace of execution is notable.

Metaplanet bought nearly 96.45 million of the 200 million shares authorized for repurchase in less than three weeks. It has deployed about 42% of the program’s maximum spending allowance.

As of Oct. 31, the company reported 1.268 billion issued common shares excluding treasury stock and approximately 96.47 million treasury shares.

The rapid buyback suggests the authorization is being treated as an active capital-management tool rather than a standby program.

Another $212 Million Is Available for Bitcoin

Metaplanet is also keeping its bitcoin acquisition capacity intact.

The company separately redeemed $50.7 million (¥8 billion) of bonds ahead of schedule using cash. Following changes to its funding allocation, about $211.7 million (¥33.422 billion) is now available for bitcoin purchases.

That creates an unusual two-sided strategy.

Metaplanet can buy bitcoin when BTC offers the better opportunity, or buy its own shares when the equity trades at an attractive valuation.

For shareholders, the metric tying both decisions together is increasingly clear: not simply how much bitcoin Metaplanet owns, but how much bitcoin each share ultimately represents.

title: Coinbase hit with 50% price target cut as post-earnings rout deepens
summary: Slowing trading activity and fallout from the Binance hack are clouding Coinbase’s revenue prospects, prompting Morgan Stanley to lower its rating on the stock.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 2, 2026

Slowing trading activity and fallout from the Binance hack are clouding Coinbase’s revenue prospects, prompting Morgan Stanley to lower its rating on the stock.

Investment bank Morgan Stanley turned bearish on Coinbase (COIN) on Monday, cutting its price target by more than half as it warned that the cryptocurrency exchange’s profits could recover more slowly than expected.

Analyst Michael Cyprys lowered the stock’s price target from $258 to $120, a cut of about 53%, citing recent trading trends, a softer revenue outlook and uncertainty in the crypto market following Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, according to a Monday report.

The bank still sees Coinbase as one of the strongest competitors in crypto but expects profits to recover more slowly than previously forecast, putting further pressure on its share price.

The downgrade comes days after Coinbase reported a roughly 34% year-over-year decline in third-quarter net revenue to $1.16 billion on Oct. 29. The exchange posted $719 million in net income, largely driven by gains on cryptocurrency investments, while adjusted net income was $78 million.

The company’s earnings sparked a selloff in crypto-linked stocks on Friday, with its shares falling more than 13% in midday trading amid the fallout from the Binance hack. Circle shares declined more than 9%, while Strategy fell about 8%.

Coinbase shares extended their losses on Monday, dropping more than 3.3% to $138 at the time of writing, according to Yahoo Finance data.

title: Solmate Discloses 1.26M SOL Custody Positions and Says It Has No Binance Exposure
summary: Solmate says its 1.26 million SOL were held with Kraken, Anchorage Digital or BitGo, offering a dated snapshot of treasury custody.
content:
TL;DR

  • Solmate’s October 30 disclosure identifies three custody providers.
  • The company said it had no accounts or exposure to Binance.
  • The statement addresses counterparty exposure, not SOL market risk.

Solmate Infrastructure has published a specific answer to a question facing crypto treasury companies after an exchange security incident: where are the assets held? In an October 30 disclosure, the company said it had no Binance accounts or exposure and identified the custodians holding its reported 1.26 million SOL.

The Form 6-K places those holdings with Kraken, Anchorage Digital or BitGo as of October 29. It is a company statement about custody at a particular time, rather than an independent audit of every position.

Asset ownership and asset access are separate questions

A corporate balance sheet can show exposure to a cryptocurrency without explaining the complete operating arrangement behind it. Investors also need to know who controls transactions, how transfers are approved and whether the company can access the assets when it needs them.

A treasury that plans to hold for years still faces shorter-term obligations. It may need cash for operating costs, collateral for financing or flexibility to respond to an unexpected event. Custody arrangements influence how quickly it can meet those needs.

Publishing the names of service providers improves the starting point for that analysis. It does not reveal the allocation among them, every account condition or the extent to which assets may be committed to another activity. Those details require additional disclosures.

A narrow exposure statement has real value

During a security event, markets can struggle to distinguish companies directly affected from those sharing only a connection to the same asset class. A precise statement can reduce that uncertainty without making broader claims about the safety of the industry.

Solmate’s accompanying release says its validator infrastructure continued to operate normally. That addresses another part of the business: the systems participating in network operations, as distinct from where the treasury tokens are held.

The distinction is useful because an operating interruption and a custody loss are not interchangeable. A company could experience one without the other. Reporting them separately makes it easier to understand what an incident has actually changed.

Multiple providers require their own controls

Using more than one custodian can reduce dependence on a single operating platform, but it also creates work. A company must reconcile several records, maintain consistent authorization rules and understand the conditions for moving assets between accounts.

A simple example is a treasury policy requiring two approvals for a transfer. That rule must be enforceable wherever assets are held, rather than exist only in an internal document. Differences among service providers can become important when staff change or an urgent transfer is requested.

There is no evidence in this disclosure of a weakness in Solmate’s procedures. The point is that naming several providers is one component of risk management, not a complete description of it. Clear allocation and operational reporting would give shareholders a fuller view.

Custody clarity leaves price exposure intact

The number of SOL held is different from the cash value available to shareholders. That value changes with the token’s price and with the company’s wider liabilities, operating costs and financing structure.

A statement that assets are accounted for therefore cannot be translated into a guarantee about equity value. Nor does an unchanged custody position establish that tokens can be sold at a particular price without affecting execution.

Solmate’s filing is useful because it answers a bounded question with named counterparties and a dated balance. Investors assessing the company can combine that information with subsequent financial reports and operating disclosures, keeping asset safekeeping, liquidity and market exposure as separate parts of the analysis.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Binance May Have Lost Around Half of 5-Year Profits to Fines and Hacks: Analysis
summary: Binance’s “cost of doing business,” including fines and hack losses, could equal more than half of the largest crypto exchange’s estimated pre-tax profits from 2021–2025. Following the largest crypto theft in history, Binance’s combined bill for fines and hack-related losses has reached around $10.7...
content:
Binance’s “cost of doing business,” including fines and hack losses, could equal more than half of the largest crypto exchange’s estimated pre-tax profits from 2021–2025.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance’s estimated $10.7 billion bill for fines and hack losses equals around 56% of its estimated 2021–2025 pre-tax profits.
  • The exchange has paid $4.34 billion in known fines and had $6.38 billion stolen in major hacks, though a substantial chunk of the funds stolen last week were frozen.
  • Binance’s shrinking asset base and the latest hack could constrain its expansion plans as competitors aggressively invest.

Following the largest crypto theft in history, Binance’s combined bill for fines and hack-related losses has reached around $10.7 billion. Meanwhile, Vetle Lunde, head of research at K33 Research, the research arm of Norwegian digital asset brokerage K33, estimates that “a back-of-the-envelope calculation puts Binance’s pre-tax profits at $19.2 billion” for 2021–2025.

“Funds are, in all likelihood, very SAFU, and being the leading casino is unimaginably profitable,” Lunde posted on X, noting that “it is quite wild that this, to some extent, reflects a cost of doing business for Binance.”

Meanwhile, losses from the record-high hack could still decrease. Around $3 billion in stolen crypto assets have been frozen, while the hunt for the remaining funds continues. It is not yet clear how much Binance might recover or when it might do so.

Additionally, Binance used half of its SAFU fund, an emergency fund for user losses, or 7,500 BTC, to cover around 9% of the losses.

More Than $4.3 Billion in Fines and $6.38 Billion in Hack Losses

Lunde’s estimate excludes Binance’s results for 2026 and all years before 2021. For context, the U.S. Department of Justice said that between August 2017 and October 2022, U.S. users alone generated more than $1.6 billion in profit for Binance. In its nine years of existence, Binance has never published consolidated financial statements covering the entire group.

However, information about fines and hacks is more transparent. In 2023, Binance agreed to pay $4.32 billion as part of a U.S. criminal settlement. Its co-founder, Changpeng Zhao (CZ), stepped down as CEO under the deal and later spent a few months in a U.S. prison. According to Bitcoin.com News calculations, Binance’s local units have received around $20 million in fines in other countries. These range from a $6.9 million penalty in Australia this year to a $750,000 fine in Turkey in 2021, bringing the total in known fines to around $4.34 billion.

Meanwhile, in addition to the $6.34 billion Binance set aside following this October’s hack, the exchange lost 7,000 BTC, worth around $41 million at the time, in a 2019 hack. Binance covered that loss through its SAFU emergency fund. Together, the two hacks involved around $6.38 billion in company funds, though as noted, the company will be able to claw back a substantial portion of frozen funds from stablecoin issuers and other exchanges.

Combined with the fines, the exchange’s “cost of doing business” now stands at around $10.7 billion. If Lunde’s estimate is correct, then this equals around 56% of Binance’s pre-tax profits for 2021–2025. Depending on Binance’s results for 2026 and the years before 2021, fines and hack-related costs could account for around half of its lifetime profits.

Bifinity Paid $124 Million in Taxes

Binance has not made its financial figures publicly available, so these calculations remain estimates. The same applies to the taxes the exchange pays. However, financial records from Bifinity, Binance’s fiat-to-crypto payments provider in Lithuania, offer some insight.

The company, which CZ owned directly from April 2023 to January 2025, operated in Lithuania from 2020 until it began winding down this year. According to public records, Bifinity generated almost €1.5 billion ($1.68billion) in revenue and earned almost €180 million ($202 million) in net profit after paying €110.8 million ($124 million) in taxes.

A Smaller War Chest Could Hinder Binance’s Expansion

The story is still developing, while Binance says it has already covered about 95% of the affected assets, and withdrawals have resumed and are stabilizing after an initial spike. Still, the crypto giant must now allocate resources to managing the crisis, which could hurt its expansion plans, especially with a potentially smaller investment war chest.

Also, as Bitcoin.com News reported, Binance’s tracked assets have fallen by more than 11% since the Oct. 29 hack, to around $128.3 billion. The decline also reflects falling crypto asset prices and the stolen funds. This is all happening at a time when competitors such as Coinbase, Kraken, and OKX are aggressively investing in expansion. What’s more, the market also appears closer to a bear phase than a confirmed bull run, potentially slowing Binance’s efforts to rebuild its reserves through future profits.

With no plans announced to publish financial statements and demonstrate the strength of its business, the market is now waiting for several developments: a more detailed incident report once the investigation is complete, an update on the more than $2.8 billion in frozen assets, information on when Binance will replenish the SAFU fund, and the results of its proof of reserves, due on Nov. 3.

Bitcoin.com News has reached out to Binance for comment and will update the article if the exchange responds.

title: Moscow Exchange to Launch Digital Currency Trading With BTC, ETH and USDT
summary:
The Moscow Exchange
plans to launch digital currency trading on December 1, 2026, allowing market
participants to trade Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether. The exchange describes the
initiative as Russia's first organised market for digital currencies.
London's trading industry is coming home!
The launch ...
content:
2026-11-02T21:26:29.789+02:00

Monday, 02/11/2026 | 19:26 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Russia expanded its derivatives market with five crypto index-linked perpetual futures.
  • Russia's new crypto rules cap unqualified investors' annual purchases at 300K rubles.

The Moscow Exchange plans to launch digital currency trading on December 1, 2026, allowing market participants to trade Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether. The exchange describes the initiative as Russia's first organised market for digital currencies.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The launch follows Russia's gradual expansion of regulated crypto trading. In September, the Moscow Exchange introduced perpetual-style futures linked to five crypto indices. Meanwhile, new legislation established licensing requirements and retail investment limits. The Bank of Russia also allowed licensed forex dealers to offer Bitcoin and Ether CFDs to qualified investors, with leverage capped at 1:10.

Moscow Exchange Gradually Opens Crypto Market

The new market will initially operate through pilot transactions. The exchange plans to connect participants gradually as they become ready. Interest has come from existing exchange members, their clients and businesses already involved in digital currency transactions for investment and settlement purposes.

Trading will use the Moscow Exchange's existing stock market infrastructure. Transactions will also be processed through the National Settlement Centre's clearing system. Trading will follow the Moscow Exchange's existing stock market schedule.

Crypto Market to Expand Beyond Three Assets

The initial offering will cover BTC, ETH and USDT. Transactions will be available in addressable and addressless formats. The exchange has not provided further details about these formats. It also plans to expand the range of digital currencies and other digital assets over time, including Russian and international instruments.

Clients will be able to use same-day and next-day settlement options from the launch date. The exchange will also offer swap transactions to help participants manage liquidity.

Retail Investors Face Purchase Limits

Retail access will depend on investor classification. Unqualified investors will have to pass a test before buying digital currencies. Their annual purchases will be limited to 300,000 Russian rubles through a single broker.

The restrictions form part of Russia's new regulatory framework for digital currencies. Qualified investors will not be subject to the same annual purchase limit for unqualified investors.

title: Devcon Opens in Mumbai This Week With Ethereum Builders Facing a Delivery Test
summary: Devcon runs November 3–6 in Mumbai. The useful signal will be which research and product ideas become testable work after the event.
content:
TL;DR

  • Devcon is scheduled for November 3–6 in Mumbai.
  • The official programme spans technical and application topics.
  • Conference proposals should be distinguished from deployed upgrades.

Ethereum’s developer community gathers in Mumbai this week for Devcon, scheduled for November 3–6. The official event site places privacy, security, open-source systems and applications among the themes of the four-day programme.

For people following Ethereum from the market side, the useful task is to separate ideas presented on a stage from changes that developers can actually test and users can eventually rely on. A conference creates a concentrated view of the work; it does not turn every proposal into a network commitment.

Research needs a path to implementation

A protocol idea can be persuasive before its operational consequences are fully understood. It may improve one property, such as transaction handling, while adding costs elsewhere, such as data storage or the difficulty of running infrastructure.

The most informative technical presentations explain those trade-offs and offer a way for others to inspect the work. A specification, reproducible benchmark or test implementation gives outside developers something they can challenge. A performance target without those materials is harder to evaluate.

There is also a sequence between research, agreement on scope, client implementation, testing and activation. A talk about one stage should not be reported as completion of the next. This matters especially when short clips circulate without the qualifications that accompanied a presentation.

Application teams test a different kind of progress

The Ethereum Foundation’s original Mumbai announcement described a gathering extending beyond protocol engineering. That wider participation matters because improvements in the underlying network only reach users through products, interfaces and operating processes.

A wallet team, for example, might need to turn a complex authorization into something a person can understand before signing. A payments developer needs to handle delayed confirmations and mistaken inputs. An institutional application needs to reconcile its blockchain records with the obligations in its legal agreements.

These are less dramatic achievements than a headline about speed, but they can determine whether an application is dependable. A credible demonstration should show what happens when the happy path breaks, including what a user sees and how the system recovers.

Coordination is part of the infrastructure

Open-source ecosystems distribute responsibility across people who do not all work for the same organization. A change can require cooperation among client teams, infrastructure operators, wallet developers and application maintainers, each with different constraints.

Bringing those groups together can shorten the distance between a proposed improvement and a clear understanding of its consequences. It can also expose disagreements that were easy to miss in a written thread. A resolved incompatibility may be a more useful outcome than another product announcement.

That kind of progress is difficult to measure through attendance figures. It becomes visible later, when documentation improves, implementations converge or a previously blocked integration starts working. The follow-up work is where a conference’s technical value is ultimately demonstrated.

What readers can assess after the event

Useful evidence will include published materials, specific engineering milestones and clearly identified owners for the next stage of a project. Readers should be able to distinguish a proposal seeking discussion from software ready for production.

For applications, the stronger indicators are working integrations and repeated use, alongside a credible explanation of costs and failure handling. A polished demonstration can establish that an idea is possible without proving that it works reliably at scale.

Devcon’s immediate importance is bringing Ethereum’s many development efforts into view at the same time. The longer-term story will depend on what survives scrutiny and becomes usable software. Neither the schedule nor a keynote provides a dependable forecast for ETH’s price.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Nvidia, Nike Join 50 Companies Blocking OKX–ICE Stock Token Push
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Nvidia, Nike Join 50 Companies Blocking OKX–ICE Stock Token Push
Fifty companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft and JPMorgan, have blocked OKX and ICE from tokenizing their shares under the SEC’s new Innovation Exemption.
This post Nvidia, Nike Join 50 Companies Blocking OKX–ICE Stoc...
content:
Fifty public companies have now objected to having their shares tokenized on OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), as the venue’s first 30-day notice window closes Tuesday.

The venue’s Oct. 30 notice added 12 objectors, including Nvidia, Costco, Nike, Micron and Reddit. They join Microsoft, Alphabet, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Walmart, Broadcom, Verizon and Intel, among others. Of the 62 companies OKXICE initially proposed to tokenize, 43, or about 69%, have objected, according to a CoinDesk tally.

The list has grown fast: nine objectors on Oct. 15, 16 on Oct. 19, 38 on Oct. 28 and 50 two days later.

How the opt-out works

The objections stem from the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” issued Sept. 17, which lets tokenized securities venues (TSVs) trade blockchain versions of U.S. stocks through automated market makers without registering as exchanges. When an unaffiliated third party tokenizes a company’s stock, the venue must notify the issuer, which then has 30 days to object in writing. Silence counts as consent, and the order offers no way to object after the window closes.

OKXICE plans 24/7 trading of tokens backed one-for-one by shares, paired against stablecoins such as USDC in permissioned pools on OKX’s X Layer blockchain.

The objecting companies have not given reasons. JPMorgan said it remains encouraged by tokenization but wants to be thoughtful about how its shares are represented and traded. “Given how easy the opt-out is, the list of objectors is likely to keep growing,” Olivia Vande Woude, head of tokenization at Ava Labs, said.

Nasdaq’s role

The fight has also taken on a competitive edge. An executive at a Nasdaq-listed company told Crypto in America that a Nasdaq representative urged the company to object and offered a call to explain why. Nasdaq declined to comment on the claim but reiterated that TSVs are not the best path to tokenization.

Nasdaq argues that venues outside the National Market System could fragment liquidity and lack real-time best-price display and consolidated-tape reporting. It is building its own issuer-centric Nasdaq Equity Token with Kraken, targeted for the second quarter of 2027.

A full-page Wall Street Journal ad urging CEOs to opt out, headlined “YOUR STOCK. THEIR TOKENS. YOUR PROBLEM.,” linked to Nasdaq’s FAQ via QR code. Conservative-leaning nonprofit Common Sense Leadership Fund paid for it. Nasdaq said it had no connection to the ad and never funded the group.

OKXICE co-chair and former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo has called the objections a “natural response.” 

“We are at the very beginning of the rollout of fundamentally different market structure,” he said last week.

For context, a tokenized stock is a blockchain token backed one-for-one by a real share, which a third party holds. OKXICE lets it trade around the clock against stablecoins like USDC. Under the SEC’s Innovation Exemption, the venue can list these tokens without the issuing company’s consent, unless the company objects within 30 days.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Pghinvestment and the Retail Investors the Market Was Not Built For
summary: The retail investor arriving today looks very little like the one most trading platforms were originally designed around. They are younger, far more likely to be based outside the traditional financial centres, and in a great many cases they came to markets through digital assets, not through a brok...
content:
Skip to content

The retail investor arriving today looks very little like the one most trading platforms were originally designed around. They are younger, far more likely to be based outside the traditional financial centres, and in a great many cases they came to markets through digital assets, not through a broker or an adviser. What they frequently do not arrive with is formal financial education.

That is not a criticism of them. It is a description of a market that opened up faster than the teaching around it did, and it leaves platforms holding a question they did not previously have to answer: what do you owe someone who is capable, motivated and underprepared all at once.

Most of the industry has answered that question with content. Webinars, glossaries, a learning tab nobody opens twice.

The more telling answer is structural. It shows up in how an account behaves, not in what the marketing says about education.

What the participation data actually shows

The World Economic Forum, in its Global Retail Investor Outlook, describes a new wave of participants drawn from groups the industry historically underserved, including younger investors and people in emerging markets, and names limited financial education and the complexity of evolving technology among the obstacles they meet. The audience is widening in exactly the places where support has always been thinnest.

The World Federation of Exchanges reaches a complementary conclusion from the market side. Reviewing retail trading across its member exchanges, it finds that retail participation improves liquidity and the depth of the order book, while stating directly that it may increase volatility and must be complemented with strong investor protection policies. More participation is only a good outcome when something is built to carry it.

Learning without paying for the lesson

This is where Pghinvestment has made a choice that reads as a product decision but functions as an educational one. Its practice environment runs on the conditions a funded account actually sees, so the pricing and execution a client meets while testing are the ones waiting for them afterwards.

That distinction matters more than it sounds. A rehearsal that flatters the trader is not neutral. It is misleading, because it produces a confidence the market never agreed to.

Experts at Pghinvestment treat that fidelity as the whole point of the feature, not a technical detail buried inside it, which is why the practice environment sits alongside the live Pghinvestment platform rather than behind a beginner label.

The Pghinvestment entry point works in the same direction. An account can be opened without committing an amount a client would genuinely miss, which turns the first months into something a person can afford to be bad at. That is a more realistic model of how trading is actually learned than any curriculum.

Participation before mastery

There is a second route through the preparedness gap, and it is the one Pghinvestment leans on hardest: it does not insist on mastery as the price of entry.

Its managed structures let someone take part while they are still learning, instead of making them wait until they are not. PAMM and MAM arrangements place capital alongside a more experienced trader while the owner keeps sight of what is happening to it, and Copy Trading mirrors selected positions as they occur.

Used well, the Pghinvestment managed structures amount to a form of apprenticeship. A client watching decisions get made on their own balance, in markets they are still reading, learns something a tutorial cannot teach. The framing from Pghinvestment is consistent with that: these structures are presented as a route into participation while understanding builds, not as a reason to stop building it.

One environment, widening scope

There is a quieter benefit in the breadth of the Pghinvestment account range. Currencies, equities, metals, indices, commodities and digital assets sit behind one login, which means a client broadening their exposure is not also learning an unfamiliar system at the same moment they are learning an unfamiliar market.

The thing that changes is the instrument, not the interface. For someone who arrived through digital assets and is now looking at metals or indices for the first time, removing that second layer of unfamiliarity is worth more than it appears on a feature comparison.

Funding runs through card, bank transfer or digital currency, with nothing added by Pghinvestment to make a deposit. Withdrawal thresholds are set low, which keeps the arrangement workable for clients operating at modest size while they find their footing.

Where this leaves the industry

Instrument counts will keep getting longer across the industry, and they will keep mattering less than how a platform behaves in a client’s first six months. The firms that come out of this period with retained clients will be the ones that planned for people learning the job while doing it. Judged on how Pghinvestment has assembled its practice conditions, its managed routes in and its entry pricing, that looks like the assumption it started from.

summary:
Interactive Brokers

London's trading industry is coming home!
Daily Average Revenue
Trades reached 4.31 million, down 4% from October 2025 but ...
content:
2026-11-02T20:16:16.689+02:00

Monday, 02/11/2026 | 18:16 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • DARTs increased 5% monthly to 4.3 million but remained lower than the same period last year.
  • Client equity fell 4% monthly to $928.6 billion, despite 19% annual growth.

Interactive Brokers reported 5.68 million client accounts at the end of October, up 34% year-on-year and 2% month-on-month, according to its latest monthly performance metrics.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Daily Average Revenue Trades reached 4.31 million, down 4% from October 2025 but up 5% from September.

Client Credit Balances Reach $180.5 Billion in October

Client equity totalled $928.6 billion, an increase of 19% year-on-year but a decline of 4% month-on-month. Client margin loan balances rose 31% annually and 2% from September to $106.8 billion.

Client credit balances, including insured bank deposit sweeps, stood at $180.5 billion, up 15% year-on-year but down 3% month-on-month. Insured bank deposit sweeps accounted for $6.2 billion of the total.

The broker reported 163 annualised average cleared DARTs per client account. Average commission per cleared commissionable order was $2.46, including exchange , clearing and regulatory fees.

Client Equity Falls 4% Monthly

In September, Interactive Brokers reported 5.6 million client accounts, $964.7 billion in client equity and approximately 4.1 million DARTs. Trading activity increased 6% year-on-year in September, while DARTs fell 4% from August.

October's figures show continued growth in client accounts and margin loans, while client equity and credit balances declined from the previous month.

IBKR Reports US Stock Execution Costs

Interactive Brokers also reported execution costs for IBKR PRO clients trading US-regulated stocks. The average US Regulation National Market System stock trade was valued at $23,670 in October.

The total cost of executing and clearing these stocks was approximately 1.1 basis points of trade value, measured against a daily volume-weighted average price benchmark. The net cost for the rolling 12-month period was 2.4 basis points.

Interactive Brokers Gives AI Tools Trading Authority

The October results follow Interactive Brokers' expansion of its AI trading services. The broker introduced IBKR Autonomous Trading, allowing eligible clients to authorise connected AI platforms to monitor more than 75,000 stocks, options and ETFs and submit supported orders on their behalf. The feature allows clients to set trading instructions and risk limits without approving each order individually.

title: Crypto Fear Index Drops to 30 After Binance Hack as Ethereum ETFs See $1B in Outflows
summary: The Crypto Fear and Greed Index has slipped into fear territory as Binance responds to a $6.3 billion security breach and US spot Ethereum ETFs record heavy October redemptions.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

The Crypto Fear and Greed Index has slipped into fear territory as Binance responds to a $6.3 billion security breach and US spot Ethereum ETFs record heavy October redemptions.

The developments highlight growing caution across cryptocurrency markets, although available data do not establish that the Binance attack directly triggered the Ethereum ETF withdrawals.

Market participants are now monitoring exchange fund flows, institutional investment activity, and cryptocurrency prices for signs of further weakness. The latest Bitcoin (BTC) market data and Ethereum (ETH) price data offer additional context as investors assess the market’s response to the latest developments.

Crypto Fear and Greed Index Falls to 30 After Binance Hack

According to CryptoQuant, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index dropped to 30 on October 30, placing market sentiment in the fear zone for the first time since mid-August. The decline followed Binance’s October 29 security breach, which resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion in unauthorized cryptocurrency withdrawals.

Bitcoin’s Fear and Greed Index fell to 30, signaling fear among investors following Binance’s record $6.3 billion hack. Source: @cryptoquant_com via X

Market sentiment had already weakened before the incident. The index fell from 68 on October 22 to 51 by October 29, indicating that investors were becoming increasingly cautious ahead of the exchange’s announcement. Its latest reading of 30 is also 26 points below the 30-day average of 56. CryptoQuant’s historical comparison places the reading below the median of 44, although it remains above the lower quartile of 26.

The FBI attributed the Binance attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group. The exchange’s preliminary investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allegedly provided attackers with access to internal systems used to authorize withdrawals. Binance said it had found no evidence that wallet private keys were exposed.

The scale of the incident triggered an industry-wide recovery effort involving blockchain intelligence firms, law enforcement agencies, and cryptocurrency issuers. Approximately $3 billion in affected assets had been located or frozen through cooperation with industry partners. Binance also said it had covered approximately $6 billion of the estimated losses through its corporate treasury, insurance resources, and Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).

The incident has also raised questions about the security of centralized cryptocurrency exchanges and their internal withdrawal systems. Brave New Coin previously examined the breach, its recovery efforts, and the exchange’s compensation commitment in its report, Binance Confirms $6.3B Security Breach, Freezes $3B in Assets and Pledges Full Compensation.

Ethereum ETFs Record More Than $1 Billion in October Outflows

Institutional investment activity has also weakened, with US spot Ethereum ETFs experiencing substantial net redemptions during October. A report citing Glassnode data identified 23 consecutive trading days of net outflows through October 30, marking the longest reported outflow streak since the funds launched in July 2024.

US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded 23 consecutive days of net outflows through late October 2026, marking their longest withdrawal streak since launching in July 2024. Source: Glassnode via X

The withdrawals extended a period of weaker demand following substantial ETF buying in August and September. October’s net outflows exceeded $1 billion, reversing the previous month’s $832.43 million in net inflows reported by SoSoValue. The pressure remained visible toward the end of the month, when US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded approximately $155.7 million in net outflows on October 30, according to Farside Investors’ daily figures.

Farside-based calculations put the full October net outflow at approximately $1.61 billion. This highlights the scale of the monthly reversal, even as some funds attracted smaller inflows during individual trading sessions.

There is, however, a difference between the reported 23-day Glassnode streak and Farside’s publicly available daily figures. Farside recorded positive aggregate inflows on October 13, October 21, and October 23, with 19 net outflow sessions among October’s 22 trading days. The 23-day figure should therefore be attributed specifically to the Glassnode-tracked series rather than treated as a universally confirmed result across all ETF flow trackers.

The figures nevertheless point to a clear deterioration in monthly demand for US spot Ethereum investment products. ETF net outflows measure the difference between money entering and leaving the funds, rather than the total amount of Ethereum traded in the broader market. They also do not identify individual investors or establish why holders are redeeming their shares.

The reversal is particularly notable because September’s positive flows followed heavy institutional accumulation during the summer. October’s redemptions indicate that demand through traditional investment products has weakened, placing additional pressure on Ethereum’s institutional investment outlook.

Binance Withdrawals Reach $4.72 Billion as Exchange Confidence Faces Pressure

The Binance incident has created another source of concern for cryptocurrency investors, with customers moving substantial amounts of capital away from the exchange after withdrawal services resumed.

According to Reuters, Binance customers withdrew a net $4.72 billion after the exchange reopened withdrawals on November 1. The outflow represented approximately 2.8% of the platform’s assets, while Binance reported that $2.7 billion had also flowed back into the exchange. The latest figure exceeds earlier estimates of approximately $3.6 billion as withdrawals continued to be processed.

Binance restored withdrawals in phases starting at 06:00 UTC on November 1, 2026, processing $4.649B outflows across 15 networks/assets by 15:30 UTC. Source: Binance via X

Binance said withdrawal activity had declined following an initial spike and was stabilizing. The exchange has also maintained that customers will not bear the financial losses associated with the security breach.

The response from market observers has been more measured than the initial withdrawal figures might suggest. Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group, told Reuters that the incident had not yet caused widespread panic among customers.

“It has not yet triggered widespread panic or a massive, concentrated withdrawal,” Sun said.

Nevertheless, the incident could influence how institutional investors, market makers, and other financial participants assess cryptocurrency exchange exposure. Security concerns are particularly relevant for organizations responsible for holding customer assets or providing liquidity across multiple trading platforms.

The wider market response has also reflected this caution. Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $643 million in net outflows on October 30, while more than $1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to reporting cited by Reuters. These developments indicate that selling pressure extended beyond Ethereum investment products and the Binance platform.

Ethereum Staking Reaches Record High Despite ETF Redemptions

Despite weaker institutional demand through spot ETFs, Ethereum’s on-chain staking activity has continued to expand. According to Bitwise’s third-quarter staking report, approximately 43.8 million ETH was locked in staking by the end of September, representing around 35.9% of the cryptocurrency’s total supply.

Ethereum staking reached a record 43.8 million ETH in Q3 2026, representing 35.9% of the total supply, according to Bitwise. Source: @BSCNews via X

Net staking inflows reached approximately 1.99 million ETH during the third quarter. This marked the sixth consecutive quarter in which more ETH entered staking than left the network. The increase also established a new record for the amount of Ethereum committed to securing the blockchain.

However, staking growth has not come without changes to investor returns. Bitwise reported that Ethereum’s annualized gross staking yield declined to 2.63% in the third quarter from 2.81% in the previous quarter. The lower yield reflects rewards being distributed across a larger pool of staked ETH.

Ethereum’s price has also remained above $2,200 despite the ETF withdrawals and broader market uncertainty. Historical market data show that ETH traded near $2,245 on October 30 before recovering toward $2,285 by November 2.

The contrasting trends suggest that different groups of Ethereum investors are responding to market conditions in different ways. Investors using exchange-traded products have reduced their exposure, while the amount of ETH committed to network staking has continued to increase.

However, rising staking activity does not establish that existing Ethereum holders are directly absorbing the coins associated with ETF redemptions. ETF flow figures and staking deposits measure separate activities, and the available data do not identify whether the same investors are participating in both.

For the broader cryptocurrency market, the next developments in exchange security, ETF demand, and Ethereum staking will remain important indicators of investor positioning. A sustained recovery in ETF inflows and the Fear and Greed Index could indicate improving confidence, while continued withdrawals would point to persistent caution across traditional crypto investment channels.

content:
2026-11-02T18:36:00.000+02:00

Monday, 02/11/2026 | 16:36 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The launch comes as Prop Firm Match faces affiliate allegations, with Apex, Tradeify and others cutting ties.
  • The company targets a December launch with firm comparisons, verified reviews and weekly rulebook checks.

Prop Firm Prestige is preparing to open an early version of its platform tomorrow (Tuesday). Users will be able to complete time-based tasks and earn points ahead of the official launch, scheduled for before December this year.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The activities, called Drops, will reward users with Loyalty Power, which can later be exchanged for free prop trading accounts and merchandise. Participants will also enter a launch giveaway, with additional entries available through the pre-launch tasks.

Prop Firm Match Loses Partners Amid Affiliate Allegations

The development comes amid the controversy surrounding Prop Firm Match, which has faced allegations of affiliate tracking misconduct. Several prop trading firms have since ended their relationships with the platform.

Apex Trader Funding terminated its affiliate relationship with Prop Firm Match and disabled its tracking codes. Tradeify also ended its relationship, citing a breach of affiliate terms. Goat Funded Trader separately terminated its affiliate partnership, while Topstep has said it is dropping its paid listing.

Prop Firm Prestige Plans Comparison Platform

Prop Firm Prestige plans to introduce its comparison platform in stages from December 2026. It says firms will be verified before listing, with information on pricing, payouts and trading rules. Rankings cannot be purchased.

Its main tool, Prop Compare, will allow users to compare up to four firms using identical account sizes. Reviews will require proof of purchase, payout or funded status.

The company says firms will undergo six checks before listing, while rulebooks will be reviewed weekly. Other features include Prestige Pay, which applies discounts at checkout, and Loyalty Power, which users can earn through reviews and purchases. The platform will be free for traders.

title: Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Deposits and Withdrawals Due to Ongoing Security Incident, Losses Estimated Near $40 Million
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Deposits and Withdrawals Due to Ongoing Security Incident, Losses Estimated Near $40 Million
Brazil’s largest crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin says customers suffered no losses, but it has not said how much was taken or when it will reopen.
This post...
content:
Brazil’s largest cryptocurrency exchange kept deposits and withdrawals suspended on Monday after a security incident in one of its systems. The shutdown left customers unable to send funds into or out of the platform while the company worked to restore operations.

Mercado Bitcoin said in a statement posted to X that it had identified and contained the incident. The company said customers suffered no losses and that no data had leaked. It described the suspension as a precaution. Its teams are investigating, tracing assets and coordinating with authorities, the company said. According to Bloomberg, the company said it would absorb all losses.

The company has not said which system was breached, how much was taken or when it will reopen. Its current statements gave no total loss figure and no timetable.

Mercado Bitcoin has since published destination addresses tied to transactions from the incident, covering Bitcoin, Ethereum-compatible networks, Solana, Stellar and Tron. It said it shared the addresses for identification and tracking purposes. Blockchain security firm Hypernative has put preliminary estimates of suspicious transfers above $40 million across several blockchains. The exchange has not confirmed that figure.

Other analysts are citing higher figures and that the sweeping is ongoing.

Stablecoin issuer Tether has entered the response. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X at 10:06 a.m. ET that the company had frozen more than 4.5 million USDT linked to the incident. Tether invested $20 million in Mercado Bitcoin back in July, when it said the exchange served 4.5 million users.

A rough week for Mercado and other exchanges

The incident comes days after one of the largest crypto thefts in recent memory. On Oct. 29, attackers reached $6.3 billion in assets at Binance after compromising an engineer’s laptop and gaining access to internal systems used to process withdrawals. 

Binance said it found no evidence that private keys were exposed. By Nov. 1, it had replaced 95 percent of the stolen assets and begun restoring withdrawals in phases.

On the law enforcement front, the FBI has attributed the attack to North Korea, and the U.S. Secret Service is working with Circle to trace and freeze funds. Tether reported about $1.57 billion in USDT frozen, and Circle said it had frozen more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with authorities. 

Binance has said it found additional points of breach beyond the initial compromise, which it originally attributed to a single engineer’s laptop. The exchange has not yet published a full post-mortem explaining how the attackers prepared and executed the operation, which some estimates suggest took at least 36 hours of groundwork. 

The destination of roughly $3.3 billion in stolen funds that were not frozen has also not been fully explained, and the exchange has not detailed what it expects to recover from that pool. Investigators continue to track wallet activity across ten blockchains.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Binance Reopens Withdrawals as Hack Recovery Enters Second Week
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance Reopens Withdrawals as Hack Recovery Enters Second Week 
Binance has reopened withdrawals after its $6.3 billion North Korea hack, covered 95% of losses, and has reserves for the remaining 5%, with post-mortem reviews to stay open.
This post Binance Reopens Withdrawals as H...
content:
Binance restarted customer withdrawals on Sunday, four days after hackers drained roughly $6.3 billion from its hot wallets in the largest crypto theft on record. 

The exchange reopened in stages over the weekend, starting with bitcoin and expanding to 15 networks. The move marked the first real test of whether the platform could absorb a loss of that size without freezing its customers out for longer.

The recovery push began Saturday. In its third recovery update, Binance said it had replenished 90% of the impacted amount with company funds. The exchange drew on part of its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury to buy replacement tokens. 

The futures fund contribution drew particular attention, since Binance described the remaining balance as a regulatory requirement. Binance also published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot dated October 31, giving users a baseline to check their balances against.

Sunday’s reopening began at 06:00 UTC with BTC. Binance then added ETH, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, XRP, Dogecoin, Tron, Polygon, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Zcash, TON and Sui. Between 06:00 and 15:30 UTC, the exchange processed about $4.65 billion in withdrawals against roughly $1.01 billion in deposits. 

That produced a net outflow near $3.64 billion, equal to about 2.1% of the $171 billion in assets Binance reported in its late-October proof of reserves.

Deposits stayed open throughout the rollout, and the exchange said temporary delays were possible during the initial surge in volume.

Binance said its Sunday update raised coverage to 95% of the impacted amount. The remaining 5% sits in less liquid tokens outside the top ten assets on its proof-of-reserves list. Sourcing those tokens at the required scale takes more time, and the exchange said it is working with industry partners and over-the-counter desks to complete the purchases. Binance has committed to covering the full amount, and it has repeated that users will not bear the financial impact of the theft.

On Monday, Binance said the full zero-knowledge proof for the October 31 snapshot is complete. Users holding BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD or ZEC can run the exchange’s verifier to confirm their balances are backed at least 1:1. 

The verifier is open source, and the exchange has pointed users to a step-by-step guide. 

The exchange plans another snapshot covering more tokens on November 4, with a proof expected to take 40 to 50 hours to generate. A further withdrawal phase is scheduled for Tuesday, and the exchange said it would share details once the rollout is ready.

Binance hack background

On the law enforcement front, the FBI has attributed the attack to North Korea, and the U.S. Secret Service is working with Circle to trace and freeze funds. Tether reported about $1.57 billion in USDT frozen, and Circle said it had frozen more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with authorities. 

The market reacted sharply to the breach. Bitcoin fell about 5% to below $77,000 in the hours after the attack, and shares of Coinbase,Robinhood, Strategy, and Strive all declined as investors weighed the risk of exchange-level losses across the sector.

Binance has said it found additional points of breach beyond the initial compromise, which it originally attributed to a single engineer’s laptop. The exchange has not yet published a full post-mortem explaining how the attackers prepared and executed the operation, which some estimates suggest took at least 36 hours of groundwork. 

The destination of roughly $3.3 billion in stolen funds that were not frozen has also not been fully explained, and the exchange has not detailed what it expects to recover from that pool. Investigators continue to track wallet activity across ten blockchains.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

summary:

content:
2026-11-02T16:01:44.582+02:00

Monday, 02/11/2026 | 14:01 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Metals made up 69% of broker volume in early third-quarter data, still more than four times the share of FX.
  • FX rose in a quarter that brought the first joint US-Japan yen intervention since 2011.

Metals contracts, led by gold, made up about 69% of retail CFD trading volume in the third quarter of 2026, preliminary FM Intelligence data show. That was down from 78% in the second quarter, while currency pairs rose to 16% from 10%.

The figures, published on Thursday, come from the brokers that have reported so far, and FM Intelligence's early reading of the quarter puts total volume about 8% above the second quarter.

Even at that pace, the market would not be back to where it started the year. Monthly retail volume fell 9.3% to $30.4 trillion in the second quarter, and an 8% rebound on that level leaves it about 2% short of the first quarter, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Metals Still Lead by a Wide Margin

The mix moved in one direction, though the ranking held. Metals lost nine percentage points and still came out more than four times larger than FX, the second-biggest category, with gold again the main instrument.

That dominance is more than a year old. Metals CFDs made up more than 60% of global broker volume in the first half of 2025, nearly 80% of it in gold, FM Intelligence data showed last October.

Read together with the 8% estimate, the new shares imply metals volume about 4% lower than in the second quarter and FX volume roughly 70% higher, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation. That holds only if the early sample matches the brokers behind the second-quarter shares.

A Quarter of Yen Intervention and Rate Hikes

The currency gain came in a quarter with three official moves on the dollar and the yen. Japan's Ministry of Finance bought yen on July 30, and the US Treasury joined the next day in the first coordinated intervention between the two governments since 2011.

In September the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time since 2023, and the Bank of Japan followed two days later. Cboe FX's USD/JPY volume rose 45.3% that month, the fastest gain among its five largest pairs.

The yen also moved more from day to day. Annualized volatility in USD/JPY was 9.0% in the third quarter against 5.4% in the second, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation from daily closing prices.

FX Starts From a Low Base

Before this quarter, the trend ran the other way. FX made up 13.7% of the monthly volume FM Intelligence tracked across a wider broker set in the second quarter, down from 26.8% a year earlier. The preliminary sample puts the same quarter at 10%.

The largest brokers trade even less of it. EC Markets, the top name in FM Intelligence's broker volumes tracker, booked about $0.06 trillion of its $2.1 trillion in average monthly second-quarter volume in currency pairs.

Listed brokers' own reports do not all follow the preliminary mix. At XTB, commodity CFDs generated 70.8% of the gross result on financial instruments in the third quarter, up from 60.5% in the second, its results showed last week. That figure measures revenue, not volume.

The full preliminary analysis also splits volume between mobile and desktop platforms, where the shift was larger than in the instrument mix. FM Intelligence will publish its final quarterly report once the remaining brokers submit their data.

title: XDC Ventures Backs ScallopX to Take XDC and USDC From Wallet to Checkout
summary: XDC Ventures (XVC Tech), the US$125 million venture capital arm of XDC Network, has made a strategic investment in ScallopX, a global fintech platform that connects traditional financial services with digital assets. Through the deal, native XDC and USDC on XDC Network will power Scallop prepaid car...
content:
2026-11-02T16:00:00.000+02:00

Monday, 02/11/2026 | 14:00 GMT by FM

Disclaimer

  • The investment brings native XDC and USDC to prepaid cards, Apple Pay and multi-currency accounts, and opens plans to explore AI agent payments

XDC Ventures (XVC Tech), the US$125 million venture capital arm of XDC Network, has made a strategic investment in ScallopX, a global fintech platform that connects traditional financial services with digital assets. Through the deal, native XDC and USDC on XDC Network will power Scallop prepaid cards, Apple Pay spending, fiat and stablecoin on- and off-ramps, multi-currency accounts and currency swaps, alongside cross-border payouts to more than 70 markets.

"Blockchain's next wave of adoption won't come from trading. It will come from people paying for groceries, businesses settling invoices and, increasingly, AI agents transacting on their behalf," says Ritesh Kakkad, Co-Founder, XDC Network. "That only happens when digital assets run on regulated, compliance-ready rails that connect to real-world payments. ScallopX gives XDC and USDC a direct path into cards, fiat accounts and cross-border payouts, and positions us for what comes next in agentic AI and ISO 20022 financial messaging."

Beyond consumer payments, XDC Ventures and ScallopX plan to explore white-label payment super apps for banks, fintechs and developers, combining fiat accounts, cards, stablecoin wallets, ISO 20022 messaging and agentic AI payments. Built on XDC Network’s fast, low-cost settlement, these would help businesses launch financial products faster and automate cross-border transactions.

Raj Bagadi, Founder and CEO of ScallopX, added, "This strategic backing from XDC Ventures is a significant catalyst. XDC’s institutional credibility and rapid innovation across RWAs and AI agent payment rails via XDC AI make them an ideal partner. Together, we are equipping enterprises, fintechs, and autonomous platforms with the tools to deploy compliant, next-generation financial services in record time."

ScallopX has publicly announced Money Services Business (MSB) registrations in the United States and Canada, alongside previously reported European virtual asset permissions, and is pursuing opportunities in key financial markets, including Hong Kong.

The deal marks XDC Ventures’ another major move into regulated financial infrastructure, following its acquisition of Contour Network last year, a trade finance platform originally backed by major international banks. Where Contour anchors XDC Network in institutional trade, ScallopX extends it to consumer and business payments, with compliance, KYC/AML standards and trusted payment infrastructure at the core of both. Together, they position XDC Network as settlement infrastructure connecting traditional finance, digital assets, global payment applications and AI-driven commerce.

title: Strategy (MSTR) Adds 811 Bitcoin, Strive (ASST) Follows Suit With 124 as Both Keep Stacking
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy (MSTR) Adds 811 Bitcoin, Strive (ASST) Follows Suit With 124 as Both Keep Stacking
Strategy bought 811 bitcoin for $65.5 million and Strive added 124 BTC last week, with the two firms together adding 935 coins and Strategy now holding 849,327 BTC.
This post Strategy (MSTR)...
content:
Strategy bought another 811 bitcoin last week. The Saylor-led firm spent about $65.5 million at an average of $80,846 per coin between October 26 and November 1, according to its 8-K filing on Monday. That brings total holdings to 849,327 BTC, bought for roughly $64.1 billion at an average of $75,451.

The money didn’t come from new preferred stock this time. Strategy sold about 1.18 million shares of MSTR common stock for roughly $164 million, sent $65.5 million into bitcoin, and parked the remaining $98.5 million in USD cash. It also spent around $208 million buying back about 2.1 million shares of its STRC preferred. 

Strategy spent much of the year leaning on preferred issuance to fund purchases, and the company is now using the buyback to tidy up its preferred stack while still adding coins.

Saylor teased the purchase Sunday with his usual tracker chart and a line that made the rounds on X: “We found room for even more orange.” 

The buy landed a few days after Strategy reported its third-quarter results on Thursday. Net income hit $19.5 billion, up from $2.79 billion a year earlier, driven by a $20.9 billion operating gain tied to the bitcoin price rising during the quarter. That gain is a paper one under fair-value accounting, not cash. Saylor called it the start of the next bitcoin bull market and pointed to bitcoin trading about 21% above its 200-week moving average. The same release said CFO Andrew Kang will step down November 5, with COO Reza Virasteh taking over the role in January. 

Strategy shareholders also recently approved a proposal allowing four preferred stocks — STRF, STRC, STRK, and STRD — to accrue dividends daily, including weekends and holidays, with 99.3% of votes cast in favor. The change was intended to improve liquidity, reduce reinvestment delays, and increase price stability, while keeping dividend rates and total obligations unchanged. The new payment schedule remained subject to board approval and regulatory filings, with implementation expected to begin in November 2026 for STRC and January 2027 for the other preferred stocks.

Strive adds bitcoin as well

Strive is still in the race for second place among public holders. The Matt Cole-run firm added 124 BTC between October 24 and 30 at about $80,526 each, lifting its stack to 43,124 BTC. 

That’s a smaller buy than its previous week, when it added more than 6,000 coins, but Cole has been consistent about his approach. He has said the company is buying “hand over fist” when prices dip, and he has framed the funding model around perpetual preferred equity as a way to avoid forced selling. 

Strive’s cash position slipped about $14 million to $490 million over the same stretch, and it still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s STRC.

Binance hack rattles both stocks 

Meanwhile, the biggest story in crypto last week wasn’t a buy. On October 29, Binance was hit by what it now estimates is a $6.3 billion security breach, one that started with a compromised DevOps laptop.

Blockchain analytics firms including Chainalysis and TRM Labs have linked the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and the drain reportedly took about 20 minutes. Binance says it has frozen roughly $3 billion of the stolen funds and will cover losses from its SAFU fund and company reserves. 

Bitcoin slid toward $76,000 on the news, and it fell about 3.6% over the week.

Strategy’s stock dropped about 9% last week and closed Friday at $130.51. The company still has about $18.6 billion of MSTR available under its ATM program, which means more buys are likely if the market cooperates.

Strive shares were down around 20% last week. At the time of writing, bitcoin is near $78,000.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

Elev8, a global CFD broker serving more than 18 million trading accounts across more than 100 countries, announces a decision to lower trading spreads for new clients who register between 22 October and 30 November 2026. Spreads on gold (XAUUSD) at Elev8 now start from 2.4 pips, down 23% from ~3.1 pips. The roll-out marks the launch of Elev8's Month of Golden Opportunities, a multi-stage promotional campaign running until 30 November 2026, with further features planned in the coming weeks.

Under the Month of Golden Opportunities campaign, Elev8 is reducing transaction costs on 12 instruments: major currency pairs, gold, the US30 index, and cryptocurrencies. Elev8's reduced spreads are available exclusively to new clients registering between 22 October 2026 and 30 November 2026.

Gold (XAUUSD) is the focus of the Elev8 campaign. Spreads on XAUUSD at Elev8 now start from 2.4 pips, down from ~3.1 pips. Building on an already competitive foundation, Elev8 further optimised gold trading conditions to deliver even tighter pricing.

Alongside gold, clients will find reduced pricing across high-demand instruments, including the Euro (EURUSD), Bitcoin (BTCUSD), and major Forex pairs:

  • XAUUSD (Gold): Starting from 2.4 pips (featuring a 23% reduction)
  • EURUSD: Starting from 0.9 pips (featuring a 31% reduction)
  • BTCUSD: Starting from 2.0 pips (featuring a 33% reduction)

In addition to primary assets, the promotional campaign reduces execution costs across a wide range of popular financial instruments, including major currencies and the US30 equity index.
